entities.desc: **Market value halves from the June peak (#146, Oct 22, 2026):** SBG fell 6.9% on Oct 22, taking it down 50% from its June 2 record and more than 30% in October, the worst performer in the Nikkei this month. Market value of about ¥24.7tn ($157bn) now sits below Hitachi and Recruit; four months earlier it briefly passed Toyota as Japan's largest company. 5Y CDS reached a near four-year high on Oct 20 (roughly 400-430bp vs ~280bp in June). Drivers: debt-funded AI exposure (about $64.6bn committed to OpenAI for ~13%, $5.4bn for ABB Robotics, $3.1bn for DigitalBridge), the record $11.1bn September junk bond at coupons up to 9.75%, CoreWeave's distressed bonds, and cheaper Chinese models pressuring OpenAI's pricing. Fitch rates SBG BB+; S&P outlook negative. **Telecom unit books a live-traffic AI-RAN trial with Nokia (#145, Oct 20, 2026):** SoftBank Corp (TSE: 9434) and Nokia agreed to test AI-RAN on SoftBank's commercial network in Japan in 2027, running Nokia's anyRAN cloud RAN software on SoftBank's AITRAS platform and orchestrator with Nvidia's Aerial RAN Computer (Grace CPU, RTX PRO 4500 GPU, ConnectX-8). The trial tests whether radio processing and AI inference can share one GPU server at carrier grade, which decides whether GPUs at cell sites can earn revenue from AI workloads. Nokia joins Ericsson, whose AI scheduler lifted spectral efficiency up to ~25% on SoftBank's live 5G network in August. The same day the parent's 5-year CDS reached a four-year high (about 430bp per GuruFocus) on AI funding strain and CoreWeave exposure, and SBG fell 6% on Oct 20 before recovering 3.5% on Oct 21. **Weighs ~$18B bid for Allied Universal to automate guarding (#142, Oct 16-17, 2026):** Bloomberg and Reuters reported SoftBank is in preliminary talks to buy Allied Universal, the largest US security services firm (owned by Warburg Pincus and La Caisse; ~$23B annual revenue; bought G4S in 2021), at up to ~$18B excluding debt (WSJ). Plan is to replace some guard tasks such as patrols, camera monitoring and access control with robots over time; Allied also staffs data center construction and operations. First large target to surface for the Gulf-funded buy-and-automate vehicle. No price or financing agreed. **OpenAI run-rate shortfall hits the stock (#136, Oct 8-9, 2026):** The FT reported OpenAI told investors annualized revenue was approaching $50B at end-September, about $20B below the ~$70B in earlier press reports; Bloomberg said OpenAI still expects $70B+ by December. SBG fell as much as 7.3% to ¥5,600 on Oct 9 and closed -3.9% at ¥5,803. SoftBank's final $10B tranche closed Oct 1, taking its OpenAI investment to ~$64.6B for ~13%, funded partly by a ¥1T retail bond and high-yield notes at up to 9.75%; the price of OpenAI's ~$1.4T pre-money round now sets SBG's NAV and loan-to-value. **Sounds out Gulf investors for up to $100B AI buyout vehicle (#133, FT Oct 9, 2026):** Son approached senior Middle East figures, including in the UAE, about a vehicle that would buy established companies and run them on AI and robotics, with robotics/physical-AI unit Roze (planned IPO) at the centre. FT named MGX and G42 as possible participants; talks preliminary, no commitments, SoftBank has not confirmed. Shifts the model from Vision Fund minority startup stakes to controlled operating businesses funded by outside capital, since the parent's balance sheet is committed to OpenAI. **OpenAI marks itself up as SoftBank's last tranche closes (#124, Sept 29-Oct 1, 2026):** OpenAI opened talks to raise at least $30B at about a $1.4T pre-money valuation, up from $852B post-money in March, after shelving its IPO. SoftBank's final $10B tranche, funded by a record high-yield bond at coupons up to 9.75%, is due October 1 and takes its commitment to about $64.6B for roughly 13%. SBG shares rose about 6% on Sept 30; SB Energy has delayed its IPO. Japan's most consequential AI investment vehicle: Vision Funds have backed 400+ technology companies globally. **AI infrastructure offensive (2025–2026):** Son has committed $500B+ in US AI infrastructure via the Stargate JV (with OpenAI, Oracle, MGX); simultaneously backing Noetra (Japan physical AI model, $6B state-backed, SoftBank consortium), SB OAI Japan GK (OpenAI exclusive Japan distribution), SB Intuitions (Japanese-language LLMs, now merged into Noetra mission), and SB Neo (US neocloud JV, Jul 2026). **ARM-SoftBank flywheel:** SoftBank's majority stake in ARM gives it unique leverage across mobile, edge, and server AI compute as the market shifts to Arm-based architectures (Apple Silicon, Nvidia Grace Hopper, AWS Graviton). The combination of AI-model bets (Noetra, SB Intuitions, SB OAI), compute bets (ARM), and infrastructure bets (Stargate) makes SoftBank the most comprehensively positioned entity in Japan's AI ecosystem. **SB Energy stake sale ahead of IPO (Aug 17, 2026):** Nvidia is investing $1.5B in SB Energy, SoftBank's US data-center developer building the 10-gigawatt Ohio campus for OpenAI, as part of a financing package that also sees Nvidia backing roughly $105B of the project's infrastructure debt (scaled back from an earlier $250B guarantee under discussion). SB Energy is targeting an IPO as soon as next month that could raise at least $5B, giving SoftBank a near-term path to monetize part of its AI-infrastructure buildout while retaining upside exposure through its remaining stake — a data point for investors tracking how SoftBank funds its OpenAI/Stargate commitments without further diluting the parent balance sheet. **Record ¥1 trillion retail bond to fund ABB robotics deal, repay OpenAI bridge loan (#85, Aug 20, 2026):** SoftBank Group finalized plans for a roughly ¥1 trillion ($6.3B) bond offering aimed at Japanese retail investors — the largest-ever retail bond sale by a Japanese company, surpassing SoftBank's own ¥600B record set in 2025 and marking its third retail bond sale this year. Seven-year notes, with a coupon expected in the upper-4% range, are earmarked for two purposes: financing the ~$5.4B acquisition of ABB's robotics division (announced Oct 2025, expected to close mid-to-late 2026) and repaying a bridge loan that backed SoftBank's stake in OpenAI. Leaning on retail debt — rather than equity monetization alone — to fund both the robotics arm of its physical-AI strategy and its OpenAI exposure underscores how central borrowed money has become to Son's AI buildout, a dynamic some analysts have flagged as a credit-strain risk if AI capex returns disappoint. **AI-native RAN validated on live 5G network (#90, Aug 20, 2026):** SoftBank Corp and Ericsson completed Japan's first live-network validation of an AI-native scheduler for link adaptation — machine-learning decisions injected directly into commercial 5G baseband equipment in real time. Results: spectral efficiency up to ~25% and downlink user throughput up to ~50% at best-performing sites, ~10% average gains across all sites tested. Distinct from SoftBank's equity-stake AI bets (Noetra, OpenAI, Stargate), this is AI built into network infrastructure SoftBank already owns — positioning ahead of 5G Advanced/6G, with monetization (licensing vs. proprietary differentiator) still an open question. Shares eased 0.56% on Aug 27 as an early Nvidia-earnings-driven rally in Tokyo chip/AI names faded into profit-taking by the close. **Record retail bond priced (#97, Sept 4, 2026):** SoftBank priced the ¥1 trillion ($6.3B) seven-year retail bond flagged on Aug 20, with the coupon set near the upper end of the previously guided 4.3–4.9% range — still Japan's largest-ever retail bond offering by any issuer. The public offering period runs Sept 7–16, with issuance Sept 17 and maturity in 2033. Proceeds remain earmarked for the ~$5.4B ABB robotics acquisition and repayment of the bridge loan behind SoftBank's OpenAI stake. The pricing is a funding-mechanics confirmation rather than a new commitment, but it is a live test of retail-investor appetite for SoftBank's AI-linked debt load at scale — a data point for the credit-strain question some analysts have raised if AI capex returns disappoint. **Record short interest collides with $25.9bn bridge-loan repayment (#105, Sept 10-15, 2026):** Short interest in SoftBank Group rose to 2.27% of float as of Sept 9 — the highest since July 2025 — with notional short value of $3.9bn, the most since S3 Partners' data began in 2015, setting up a potential short-squeeze dynamic if bearish positions are forced to cover into further rallies. The timing is pointed: SoftBank drew $30bn of a $40bn bridge facility in March to fund its OpenAI stake and is set to repay the remaining $25.9bn balance on Sept 15, with a prospective $10-20bn high-yield bond offering under consideration to refinance the facility with longer-term debt — on top of the ¥1tn retail bond and roughly $25bn already raised across bond and margin-lending markets in 2026. The convergence of record short bets, a hard Sept 15 repayment deadline, and a crowded high-yield calendar is the clearest market-structure test yet of whether SoftBank's debt-fueled AI-investment strategy (OpenAI, Stargate, ABB robotics, Noetra) can keep refinancing itself at scale without triggering the credit-strain concerns analysts have flagged since the Aug 20 retail bond. **Two-day rout on Anthropic/OpenAI AI-safety warnings, lands on bridge-loan repayment day (#108, Sept 14-15, 2026):** Shares fell as much as 13% Monday and a further 10.7% intraday Tuesday after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a Sept 12 essay calling for a deliberate slowdown (減速, gensoku) in frontier AI development, a position OpenAI's Sam Altman publicly backed over the weekend along with confirming OpenAI will not IPO in 2026. The Nikkei 225 fell nearly 2% Monday and touched a six-week low near 63,000 Tuesday before closing down ~0.9% at 63,492. The reaction lands on the same day SoftBank is due to repay the $25.9bn balance of its OpenAI bridge loan — meaning an AI-safety-driven equity repricing and a hard refinancing deadline are hitting simultaneously, a pointed test of whether debt markets keep extending credit at the pace SoftBank's AI strategy requires. Morningstar's Dan Baker attributed the move to investors pricing in the chance regulators slow AI development, rather than any SoftBank-specific news. **Apollo weighs raising NAV loan to $9bn to fund OpenAI stake (#111, Sept 17, 2026):** Bloomberg reported Apollo Global Management is in talks to boost the size of a net-asset-value (NAV) loan to SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 to $9bn from $5.4bn, with the financing backed by Vision Fund 2 assets rather than SoftBank's parent balance sheet directly. Apollo first made the loan in 2021 and had already raised it by $900mn to $5.4bn last year; size and terms of the latest increase remain unfinalized, and both companies declined to comment. The talks come on top of SoftBank's already-disclosed $64.6bn OpenAI commitment and the $10bn OpenAI-holding-backed loan (including Apollo among lenders) raised in August -- meaning a fourth distinct debt instrument (NAV loan, OpenAI-holding-backed loan, ¥1tn retail bond, and the now-repaid $40bn bridge facility) is under active expansion, reinforcing the pattern of SoftBank layering multiple, differently-collateralized borrowing structures to keep funding its OpenAI/Stargate exposure rather than drawing down equity. **Record $11.15bn jumbo bond to fund third OpenAI tranche (#115, Sept 21, 2026):** SoftBank Group launched $10bn and €1.15bn (~$1.35bn) of senior unsecured notes -- split into 3.5-, 5.5- and 7.5-year dollar tranches and 4- and 6-year euro tranches -- per a term sheet circulated Sept 21. If completed at the marketed size, it would be the largest Asia-Pacific non-financial corporate bond deal on record, surpassing 7-Eleven's $10.93bn 2021 sale. Proceeds fund SoftBank's $10bn payment for the third tranche of its follow-on OpenAI investment, expected to close Oct 1, plus general corporate purposes. The deal is the fifth distinct debt instrument SoftBank has tapped in 2026 to fund its OpenAI/Stargate exposure -- after the now-repaid $40bn bridge facility, the ¥1tn retail bond, the OpenAI-holding-backed loan, and the Apollo NAV loan -- underscoring that public bond markets, not just bank and retail debt, are now absorbing SoftBank's AI-investment funding needs at record scale. **Bond priced at up to 9.75% to fund final OpenAI tranche (#121, Sept 24, 2026):** SBG priced $10bn of dollar notes (2030 8.625%, 2032 9.25%, 2034 9.75%) and EUR1bn of euro notes (7.125%, 8.0%), about JPY1.76tn in total and the largest high-yield corporate deal on record. Settlement Sept 29; proceeds fund the final OpenAI tranche due Oct 1, after which unused bridge-loan capacity is cancelled. Total OpenAI commitment reaches $64.6bn for roughly 13%. SBG has issued $14.6bn of high-yield bonds in 2026 (63% of APAC/Japan HY supply); CDS above 400bp vs ~280bp in June; shares fell 3.2% on Sept 25 while the Nikkei rose. **SAIMEMORY picks Shinko for ZAM packaging (#123, Sept 28, 2026):** SoftBank's memory subsidiary signed a basic agreement with Shinko Electric Industries to develop packaging and manufacturing processes for Z-Angle Memory, its Intel-based HBM alternative; prototypes FY2027, practical use FY2029. **CoreWeave debt scare (#139, Oct 15, 2026):** fell about 9.4% by midday as CoreWeave's bonds traded at distressed levels; SoftBank's own $11bn of September high-yield notes at 9.75% and its OpenAI stake make it the most direct Tokyo proxy for AI financing risk.

entities.name: NEC Corporation
entities.desc: Japan's leading enterprise IT services provider with deep government relationships. NEC's AI portfolio spans facial recognition (ranked #1 globally by NIST FRVT for several years), natural language processing, and digital twin platforms. **'Corporate AI & Workforce Division': first all-AI department (#83, Aug 10, 2026):** NEC announced it had formally established a new department, effective Aug 1, in which every role from division head to staff is filled by an AI agent rather than a human. Seventeen named AI agents — organized into four tiers (AI Division Head, AI Board, AI Managers, AI Employees) — handle tasks like sales-dashboard updates and extracting action items from meeting minutes, and can autonomously spin up new AI agents to respond to requests from other departments; humans retain final decision-making, quality control, and performance evaluation. **ITU-T standardizes AI-era network framework (#84, Aug 21, 2026):** NEC, alongside NTT, KDDI, Fujitsu subsidiary 1Finity, Rakuten Mobile, Oki Electric, and Sumitomo Electric, announced that the ITU-T (International Telecommunication Union) approved as Recommendation Y.3335 a framework the seven companies co-developed for low-latency, energy-efficient network paths across different operators — a technical building block for the All-Photonics Network (APN) that Japan's Beyond 5G/6G strategy positions as core infrastructure for physical AI (robotics, remote sensor processing). The standard, approved Aug 13 and announced Aug 21, gives NEC and its telecom-equipment peers an early lead in exporting Japan-originated network architecture as a global standard ahead of a follow-on ITU-T functional-architecture Recommendation targeted for October 2028. **Anthropic camp / 'Japanese-style AI' (Aug 14, 2026):** Nikkei Asia reported NEC, alongside Fujitsu and Hitachi, is partnering with Anthropic to promote a security- and reliability-first AI development posture for critical infrastructure and government systems — a distinct competitive camp from the NTT Data/SoftBank-OpenAI push toward scale and innovation, as Japan's top IT firms target a shift to AI-led software development by 2030. **MHI defense/AI-sovereignty strategic alliance MOU (#99, Sept 2, 2026):** NEC and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries signed an MOU for a strategic partnership in the defense sector, agreeing to deepen collaboration on operation plans, command-and-control systems, and unmanned assets, with the explicit stated goal of reinforcing Japan's industrial base for defense and establishing 'data and AI sovereignty.' NEC President Takayuki Morita framed it as a step toward 'a truly sovereign and highly reliable defense system' combining Japan's technologies and domain expertise; MHI's Eisaku Ito used identical sovereignty language. The deal extends NEC's government-facing AI portfolio (already spanning facial recognition, the all-AI Corporate AI & Workforce Division, and the ITU-T Y.3335 network standard) into defense command-and-control — a segment where AI-assisted decision systems for unmanned assets are becoming a core national-security procurement category as Japan's Ministry of Defense modernizes. **Kotoba-1 (Japanese LLM):** Developed with NVIDIA as part of Japan's domestic LLM push. Part of the Noetra consortium (SoftBank, Sony, Honda, NEC) — contributing large-scale model training expertise and enterprise distribution.

entities.name: Fujitsu
entities.desc: Japan's largest IT services company, repositioning from labor-intensive systems integration toward AI infrastructure, quantum and AI-augmented services. **MONAKA CPU goes on sale globally (#110, Sept 14, 2026):** standalone sales of the 144-core, Arm-based, 3D-stacked MONAKA CPU and MONAKA servers start November 2026, shipments from April 2027; dies are made at TSMC today, with Rapidus flagged as the future domestic source (#89). **New Mexico quantum research center (#135, Oct 8-9, 2026):** three-year MOU with the State of New Mexico, the Quantum New Mexico Institute and NMSU covering quantum hardware, software and algorithms, hybrid quantum-classical work on MONAKA-based HPC, and possible joint research with Sandia and Los Alamos. No financial commitment or site named; the state has appropriated $300M+ for quantum this year. Home roadmap with RIKEN: 256 qubits (Apr 2025), 1,000 qubits planned FY2026, 10,000+ physical / 250 logical qubits by FY2030. **Active cyber defense as a service line (#91, #122, Sept 25, 2026):** packaged dark-web monitoring (via KELA), attack surface management and threat hunting for critical-infrastructure operators as Japan's Active Cyber Defense law took effect Oct 1.

entities.name: Sony AI
entities.desc: Sony's dedicated AI research arm, positioned at the intersection of AI and creative industries. **GT Sophy:** AI agent that defeated professional esports drivers in Gran Turismo at superhuman level (Nature paper, 2022) — one of the highest-profile real-world AI sports victories. **AI imaging:** Sony's CMOS image sensors (70%+ global market share) are the primary data input for vision-AI systems globally; Sony AI is developing neural image processing that keeps sensor and AI model development tightly linked. **Noetra consortium:** Sony is a founding investor in Noetra alongside SoftBank, NEC, and Honda — contributing its sensor/imaging data infrastructure and entertainment AI expertise to Japan's sovereign physical-AI foundation model initiative.

President: Hiroaki Kitano, a pioneering AI researcher also known for RoboCup co-founding. Focuses on AI for entertainment, gaming, imaging, and creative industries.

entities.name: Preferred Networks (PFN)
entities.zh: プリファードネットワークス
entities.desc: Japan's most vertically integrated private AI company: it designs its own MN-Core accelerators, trains the PLaMo Japanese models from scratch, and sells into factories through Toyota, Fanuc and MHI. **MN-Core and the IPO plan (#102, #116, Sept 2026):** PFN is targeting a 2028-2030 IPO to fund MN-Core mass production, with customer samples in H1 2027 and a commercial launch in December 2027; MN-Core 2 went live inside its Matlantis materials simulator in September, its first deployment in a paying product. **MHI capital alliance (#114, Sept 16, 2026):** Mitsubishi Heavy Industries invested ¥10bn for AI in infrastructure and defense-adjacent machinery. **PLaMo tied into a national safety-testing platform (#139, Oct 14, 2026):** NICT, PFN and Sakura Internet said they will put NICT's 能動的評価基盤 (active evaluation platform) into service from next fiscal year. NICT and PFN co-built a 200-billion-parameter model for the platform, PLaMo 3.0 Prime (on sale since June 22) came out of that joint research, and PFN will integrate it into the platform. The Digital Agency already uses PLaMo.

entities.name: NTT Research
entities.desc: Long-horizon fundamental research division of NTT Group, focused on physics-inspired AI, cryptography, and quantum computing. **Coherent Ising Machine (CIM):** NTT Research pioneered the CIM — a photonic computing approach that converts combinatorial optimization problems into laser oscillator networks, potentially solving problems that are intractable for classical computers. Key partnership: Stanford University (YAQU quantum computing center). NTT Research's mandate is to make bets 5–20 years out rather than optimize for near-term product cycles — an unusual posture in Japan's corporate R&D landscape that is increasingly valued as the AI research horizon extends.
entities.bio: NTT Research, Inc. (founded 2019, Sunnyvale CA) is the global research arm of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation (NTT), Japan's largest telecoms company (founded 1985, listed TSE 9432; market cap ~¥14T). Focuses on fundamental research in physics, cryptography, and AI that may take 5–20 years to commercialize.

entities.name: NTT Corporation
entities.desc: Japan's largest telecoms company and parent of the NTT Group, distinct here from its NTT Research (fundamental physics/crypto R&D) and NTT Data (IT services/systems integration) subsidiaries tracked separately in this landscape — this entry covers the parent's core commercial network-infrastructure business, centered on IOWN (Innovative Optical and Wireless Network, 革新的光無線ネットワーク), NTT's next-generation all-optical computing and communications architecture. **IOWN/APN adopted for AI-enabled SDF command network (#94, Aug 30, 2026):** Nikkei reported Japan's Ministry of Defense will adopt IOWN's All-Photonic Network (APN, オールフォトニクス・ネットワーク) as the core transport layer connecting Self-Defense Forces units and bases nationwide, carrying radar, sensor, and drone data to command centers and data centers for AI-assisted analysis. The adoption will be written into the next National Defense Program Guidelines, with related costs folded into the FY2027 defense budget request and full-scale operation targeted from FY2028 — a significant government-infrastructure win for IOWN commercialization. NTT shares rose on the report. **ITU-T APN standardization:** NTT co-developed, with NEC, KDDI, and others, the ITU-T Y.3335 framework for low-latency, energy-efficient cross-operator network paths — a technical building block for APN as Japan's Beyond 5G/6G strategy positions it as core infrastructure for physical AI (robotics, remote sensor processing).

entities.name: Noetra (Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co.)
entities.zh: 日本AIファウンデーションモデル開発 / Noetra
entities.desc: Japan's state-backed foundation-model company, renamed from Japan AI Foundation Model Development on June 1, 2026 and operating since July 1. **Know-how strategy (#129, Oct 5, 2026):** President Hironobu Tamba opened Nikkei's GenAI/SUM 2026 arguing that operational know-how held by Japanese companies is Japan's winning path in AI. Noetra is building a multimodal 'mothership' model covering language, image, audio, video, sensor data and a world model, from which members will distill smaller task models; open weights are planned. Tamba says reliance on foreign models risks being cut off and that second-tier models give second-tier results. **Funding and coalition:** METI allocated ¥387.3bn for FY2026, with up to about ¥1tn over FY2026-2030 subject to annual stage-gate reviews. Shareholders number 44, led by SoftBank, NEC, Sony Group and Honda plus the three megabanks and Nippon Steel; about 28 are manufacturers. Large multimodal model targeted by 2028, commercial deployment around 2030. Risk: the data edge depends on competing shareholders actually sharing process data, and the first stage-gate review comes before any model ships.

entities.bio: Founded 2026, Tokyo, by a consortium of SoftBank, Sony, NEC, and Honda; CEO: Hironobu Tamba (also former CEO of SB Intuitions until February 2026). Japan's state-backed physical AI foundation model initiative, supported by approximately $6B in government funding under METI's AI framework. Mission: develop Japan's sovereign large-scale physical AI model — a Japan-specific LLM with robotics/embodied AI capabilities.

entities.name: Rapidus
entities.desc: Japan's state-backed attempt to make 2nm logic at home, using IBM-licensed gate-all-around technology at its IIM-1 fab in Chitose, Hokkaido. **Equity to unlock ¥2tn of bank loans (#144, Oct 19-20, 2026):** METI told the Fiscal System Council's FILP subcommittee it will request a further ¥400bn of government equity through the industrial investment program (¥150bn in FY2027, already in the budget request, ¥150bn in FY2028, ¥100bn in FY2029), taking cumulative state equity to ¥650bn after ¥100bn in FY2025 and ¥150bn in FY2026. The money is meant to lift Rapidus's equity ratio to the level lenders require before it borrows a planned ¥2tn from banks, starting with about ¥400bn in FY2027. Council members asked for a yearly review of policy need and profitability. Plan milestones: 2nm volume in FY2027, advanced packaging volume in FY2028, positive operating cash flow in FY2029, positive free cash flow and an IPO around FY2031. **Customer push: Rapidus CORE (#129, Oct 5, 2026):** signed 17 Design Solution Associates (Synopsys, Cadence, DNP, TOPPAN, Infosys, Wipro, HCL and others) to do design work for prospective customers and route them to the fab. No volume customer has been named, and a 2nm design costs roughly 15x a 28nm one. **Capacity:** CEO Atsuyoshi Koike targets about 6,000 wafer starts a month initially, rising toward 25,000 by 2028, with 1.4nm development aimed at 2029. Total state support including subsidies is reported near ¥3tn against investment needs above ¥7tn.

entities.bio: Founded August 2022, Tokyo, by a consortium of eight major Japanese companies (Toyota, NTT, Sony, Softbank, Kioxia, Denso, NEC, and MUFG) with METI backing. entities.name: TSMC JASM (Kumamoto)
entities.desc: Japan's most significant semiconductor manufacturing investment in decades and, after METI's October 2026 approval, the site of Japan's first 3nm chip production. **METI approves 3nm for Fab 2 (#143, Oct 16, 2026):** METI approved TSMC/JASM's revised plan for the second fab in Kikuyo Town: 3nm logic only, first phase of 6,000 wafers/month, first shipments by December 2028 (original plan: 6-12nm plus 40nm at 48,000 wafers/month). The subsidy cap fell from ¥732B to ¥645.15B (~$4.1B) to match the smaller phase; METI will request more in the FY2027 budget if TSMC expands. Fab 2 investment >$15.7B; TSMC puts both fabs above $23B; total public support could exceed ¥1T. METI also approved a smaller Fab 1 plan: 12-16nm dropped, 45,000 wafers/month of 22-28nm (vs 55,000 planned). **Fab 1 (volume production since Feb 2024):** mature-node logic for Sony image sensors and automotive/industrial customers, backed by ¥476B in METI subsidies. **Kumamoto 'Silicon Island' cluster:** 800+ supply-chain companies, record Taiwan-to-Japan investment approvals (128 cases in 2025), Air Liquide's €170M+ gas plants for a Kyushu logic expansion (#128) and a Kumamoto Science Park under construction. The 3nm switch gives Sony, Denso, Toyota and Japanese AI chip designers a domestic leading-edge source and puts TSMC in direct competition with Rapidus for Japanese design wins.

entities.name: Tokyo Electron (TEL)
entities.desc: **CFO points to a record ¥1tn operating profit (#132, Oct 6, 2026):** CFO Hiroshi Kawamoto (川本弘) told Nikkei Asia that operating profit should rise about 60% to a record ¥1tn in the year to March 2027, helped by price increases as well as volume. H1 guidance was raised on Jul 30 to ¥1.62tn sales and ¥458bn operating profit; TEL sees wafer-fab equipment spending above $150bn in 2026 and $190bn in 2027, and targets a 50% gross margin early in FY3/2028. Shares fell 2.38% on Oct 7 as the TELWY ADR split took effect; Q2 results are due Oct 30. **SEAJ: August Japan-made tool sales hit a record (#127, late Sept 2026):** Japan-made chip equipment sales (3-month average) reached ¥597.9bn in August, +47.4% y/y and +7.5% m/m, the highest monthly figure since records began in 1986 and the eighth straight y/y gain, driven by HBM/DRAM and TSMC advanced-logic spending. SEAJ's July forecast sees FY2026 at ¥6.55tn (+26%), FY2027 ¥7.40tn (+13%), FY2028 ¥7.77tn (+5%). TEL is the largest contributor to the series. Japan's semiconductor equipment bellwether and the world's #3 equipment maker — a critical node in the global fab supply chain. **Record FY2026 results, FY2027 H1 guidance beats consensus by 33% YoY (#101, Sept 7, 2026):** TEL's FY2026 net sales hit a record ¥2.443 trillion ($15.7B) at a 25.6% operating margin; FY2027 first-half guidance of ¥1.57 trillion (33% above the prior-year period) came in well ahead of the ¥1.42 trillion analyst consensus. TEL is investing ¥104 billion ($667M) in a new production building at its Miyagi Prefecture facility for plasma-etch and other equipment, due for completion in 2027 — management's clearest capital-allocation signal yet that it views the current AI-driven demand cycle as structural rather than transitory. The company's five largest customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix, Micron) represent roughly 55% of revenue, all mid-expansion for AI capacity; China has fallen to ~35% of revenue from a FY2024 peak of ~42% as export-control scope widens. The guidance beat is also cited (via Japan's Cabinet Office Business Conditions Index, which logged a fourth consecutive 'Improving' reading in July 2026 on the back of semiconductor-equipment order flow) as a direct structural input into Japan's national growth statistics — and, via that same BCI print, into the case for a BOJ rate hike at the Sept 17-18 meeting. **Third round of export controls takes effect (Aug 1, 2026):** METI's May 29, 2026 revision to the FEFTA control list added, for the first time, complete equipment for the entire advanced-packaging chain — not just front-end wafer fabrication tools — effective August 1. This is the third major tightening since the original July 2023 controls and directly targets the CoWoS/SoIC-style advanced packaging China's fabs need to compensate for restricted access to leading-edge lithography. TEL, along with Screen Holdings, Disco, and Kokusai Electric, already saw China sales fall sharply after the first two rounds; the new packaging-equipment scope closes off one of the remaining channels Chinese customers had been using to backfill capability, but China still accounted for roughly a third of TEL's revenue as of FY2024, so the move cuts both ways — squeezing a major customer base even as it protects the technology gap Japan's equipment makers rely on for pricing power elsewhere. **AI capex beneficiary:** Each generation of leading-edge AI training chip (TSMC N3/N2/A16, Samsung SF2) requires new TEL etch and deposition equipment purchases. TSMC's Kumamoto Fab 1 and 2 are direct TEL revenue events. **HBM equipment:** High Bandwidth Memory production requires specialized thermal processing equipment where TEL has strong positioning — a structural tailwind from AI chip demand for HBM stacks. **Order-book confirmation via Reuters Tankan (#81, Aug 11-12 2026):** The monthly Reuters Tankan survey (fielded Jul 29–Aug 6) showed Japan's manufacturer sentiment index climbing to +18 in August from +13 — the highest since March — driven almost entirely by semiconductor-linked demand: the chemicals sub-index jumped to +33 from +23 and metal/machinery to +25 from +12. A precision-machinery respondent reported receiving 'twice the normal volume of orders, an unprecedented situation.' It's independent, forward-looking confirmation of the same AI-capex order flow TEL has been citing in guidance. **Nikkei selloff on Hormuz oil risk (Aug 18 2026):** TEL shares fell 2.9% as the Nikkei dropped 1.6% to 68,098.54 after a US-Iran ceasefire lapsed and crude spiked on renewed Strait of Hormuz disruption, pushing the 10-year JGB yield to a fresh three-decade high near 2.95% — a reminder that TEL's valuation remains sensitive to macro/rate swings even as underlying chip-equipment demand strengthens. **Repeat selloff as JGB yield tops 3% (#95, Sept 1, 2026):** TEL fell 3.4%, the single biggest drag on the Nikkei 225, as the 10-year JGB yield pushed above 3% for the first time since 1996 and renewed Middle East-linked oil gains revived the same inflation/rate-discounting dynamic that hit the stock on Aug 18. Advantest fell 1.6% alongside it. The move is a valuation story rather than a demand story — nothing in TEL's underlying order book has changed since its record Q1 FY2027 guidance (Jul 30) or the Aug 12 Reuters Tankan confirmation of AI-linked capex strength — but it underscores that TEL's re-rating over 2026 has made the stock a high-beta proxy for JGB yield moves, not just chip-cycle sentiment. **September Reuters Tankan: electronics sentiment hits a new high (#104, Sept 9, 2026):** The Reuters Tankan poll (fielded Aug 26-Sept 4) showed the manufacturer sentiment index at +21, its highest since December 2021, with the electronics sub-index -- the one most directly tied to TEL's customer base -- surging to +39 from +24 the prior month on AI-linked semiconductor and data-center demand. It's the third consecutive monthly Reuters Tankan reading (following Aug 12's +18) confirming the same order-flow strength TEL has been citing in its own guidance, this time from an independent survey rather than TEL's internal numbers. **Two-day slide as AI-safety warnings compound oil-driven rate jitters (#108, Sept 14-15, 2026):** TEL fell 2.6% Monday and a further 1% Tuesday as Anthropic/OpenAI AI-safety warnings (see SoftBank) and a fresh oil-price jump after Saudi Arabia shut a major pipeline revived the same inflation/rate-discounting dynamic that hit the stock on Aug 18 and Sept 1. Nothing in TEL's own order book changed — the move sits against, not on top of, the Sept 7 guidance beat and the Sept 9 Reuters Tankan record — but it is a fresh instance of the stock trading as a high-beta proxy for both global AI-capex sentiment and JGB-yield moves simultaneously, two external variables converging in the same week as the Sept 17-18 BOJ meeting. **Bengaluru India R&D site announced (Sept 19, 2026):** TEL is opening a software-development site in Bengaluru focused on equipment design and simulation, and plans joint research with Indian universities on next-generation semiconductor technologies — part of a broader wave of Japanese materials/equipment firms (Fujifilm, Sumitomo Chemical, Hirata) deepening ties with India's semiconductor buildout at Semicon India 2026. This is R&D/software work, not a manufacturing shift, and sits alongside (not in place of) TEL's ¥104bn Miyagi production-building expansion. **Gujarat semiconductor training center backed by METI (#114, Sept 19-20, 2026):** At Semicon India 2026, Tokyo Electron confirmed plans to open a dedicated semiconductor training center in Gujarat in 2027 to build a fab- and equipment-engineer talent pipeline for India's expanding chip industry, under a METI-selected HR-development-ecosystem project distinct from the software-and-simulation R&D site TEL is separately opening in Bengaluru (#113). The training center is a government-cost-shared workforce play rather than a capacity or revenue commitment — TEL's return is a trained local labor pool and preferred-vendor positioning as India's incentive-backed fabs (Tata Electronics' Dholera plant among them) move from construction to hiring, a slower-moving but genuinely incremental variable layered on top of the Bengaluru R&D site and the ¥104bn Miyagi production-building expansion tracked in recent issues. **CoreWeave shock (#139, Oct 15, 2026):** fell about 7% by midday as the Nikkei lost 3,318 points on fears about AI data-center financing, a smaller drop than test, wafer and inspection peers. TSMC the same day reiterated $60-64bn of 2026 capex and said 2026-2028 spending would be significantly higher than the prior three years, which supports TEL's order book ahead of its Oct 30 results.

entities.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
entities.desc: An upstream semiconductor materials monopoly, largely invisible to the AI narrative but critical to it. Shin-Etsu's semiconductor-grade silicon wafers are the substrate on which virtually every chip in this landscape is made. **Market position:** With SUMCO, Shin-Etsu holds a combined ~60% of the global silicon wafer market — a near-duopoly on the most upstream critical semiconductor input. **AI demand impact:** Each new AI training fab (TSMC N2 at Kumamoto, Intel 18A, Samsung SF2) directly increases silicon wafer demand. Shin-Etsu's pricing power in a constrained wafer market gives it structural upside in any AI-driven capex cycle. **Rare-earth magnets:** A significant second business line — permanent magnets are critical for EV motors and humanoid robot actuators, two categories growing at AI-driven pace. **China rare-earth curbs squeeze magnet inputs (#82, Aug 17, 2026):** Japan imported just 13 tons of dysprosium (ジスプロシウム) in 1H26, down 82% YoY, with zero imports recorded in four of the first six months; yttrium imports fell 74% to 204 tons. European dysprosium prices have risen roughly sevenfold since China's April 2025 export controls took effect, and China's overall rare-earth shipments to Japan fell 43.8% YoY as of June even as shipments to the Netherlands (home to ASML) surged 121.4%. Dysprosium is essential to the high-performance permanent magnets Shin-Etsu supplies for EV and hybrid motors, while yttrium coats chipmaking equipment components — meaning the squeeze hits both of Shin-Etsu's core AI-adjacent businesses at once. Japan is diversifying supply (yttrium now sourced from 12 non-China countries in 1H26) and expanding recycling, but alternative volumes remain far short of what's needed to replace China as the dominant supplier. **China imposes anti-dumping deposits up to 99.2% on Japanese DCS (#102, Sept 9, 2026):** China's Commerce Ministry imposed provisional anti-dumping deposits of 80.8–99.2% on dichlorosilane (DCS) imports from Japan effective Sept 8, following a probe opened in January 2026 that found Japanese DCS dumping had caused material injury to domestic producers. Shin-Etsu and Denal Silane are named exporters; Shin-Etsu shares fell 3.4% in Tokyo on the news while Chinese rivals Tangshan Sunfar Silicon and Hubei Heyuan Gas jumped their 10% daily limit. DCS is a specialty gas used in chemical-vapor-deposition steps for logic and memory chips, and Japan is the leading global producer of the ultrapure grade. Shin-Etsu said any revenue impact would not be significant, but the measure — layered on top of the existing rare-earth/dysprosium supply squeeze — adds a second front of China-directed trade friction against a company sitting at the top of the global wafer and specialty-materials supply chain. **Named alongside SUMCO in a broker's wafer-supercycle thesis; renegotiating existing contracts upward (#118, Sept 22, 2026):** The broker kept a Buy rating on Shin-Etsu as part of the same research note arguing 12-inch wafer prices need to rise 40-50% industry-wide to justify new capacity against utilization climbing from 84% (2026) toward 99% (2028). Distinct from SUMCO's public capacity-discipline stance, Shin-Etsu is reported to be actively renegotiating prices under contracts already in force, citing higher electricity, raw-material, and logistics costs -- a live repricing action rather than forward guidance. Shin-Etsu and SUMCO together control more than half of the global wafer market and the strongest share of advanced 300mm epitaxial supply, the segment AI-linked demand needs most; wafers are only 3-5% of total chip manufacturing cost, which limits how much pushback chipmakers can credibly offer.

entities.name: Ajinomoto
entities.desc: A food and seasonings company that, almost by accident of its amino-acid chemistry business, controls one of the most concentrated chokepoints in the global chip-packaging supply chain. **ABF near-monopoly (#93, Aug 19-31, 2026):** Ajinomoto derived ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film) — the insulating build-up film used in nearly every high-end chip package, including the FC-BGA substrates under Nvidia, AMD, and Intel AI accelerators — from its amino-acid chemistry in the 1990s, and now holds over 95% of the global market; China's domestic self-sufficiency sits below 5%. **Reported 30% supply cut to China (Aug 19, 2026):** Chinese outlet JW Insights reported, citing unnamed supply-chain sources, that Ajinomoto has told mainland Chinese customers (Shennan Circuits, Xingsen Technology, Shenghong Electronics) it will cut ABF supply by roughly 30%, prioritizing Japanese and core overseas accounts as production runs at full utilization (~2M sqm/month). The move follows China's January restriction on rare-earth exports to Japan-linked military end users and an 82% YoY drop in Japan's dysprosium imports from China — giving the ABF cut what one report called 'obvious retaliatory optics,' even though every account attributes it to AI-driven capacity allocation rather than policy. **Confirmed price hike, unconfirmed volume cut:** A roughly 30% ABF price increase (notified to substrate makers in May, effective this quarter) is confirmed; the 30% volume cut is not. Ajinomoto has committed ¥25bn since 2023 to expand capacity ~50% by 2030, with a third plant (Kani City, Gifu) not expected online until ~2032 — meaning near-term supply stays structurally tight regardless of the allocation dispute. Goldman Sachs forecasts the global ABF supply-demand gap widening from ~10% in 2H26 to 42% by 2028.

entities.name: Shimizu Corporation
entities.desc: One of Japan's largest general contractors and the construction industry's most advanced physical-AI adopter, driven by a severe skilled-labor shortage on Japanese job sites. **Prox Industries builds behavioral-learning platform (#87, Aug 19, 2026):** Startup Prox Industries disclosed it provided fiscal-2025 technical support to Shimizu's humanoid-robot R&D, building a simulation environment on NVIDIA Isaac Sim, collecting motion data via teleoperation, and advising on Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model applications — the data-generation backbone Shimizu needs to move robots from single pre-programmed tasks toward autonomous, multi-task decision-making on site. Shimizu is separately field-testing a humanoid at the Tokiwabashi project (set to become Japan's tallest building), navigating at 1.0 m/s on a camera-equipped inspection route, with Sony as a technical partner and a stated goal of having robots learn painting and plastering from human workers by around FY2030. **Why it matters:** unlike single-purpose construction robots that Shimizu's own engineers describe as having been abandoned after proving slower and less accurate than human labor, the AI-driven approach targets a general-purpose platform across multiple job types — a bet that foundation-model-style learning transfers from Japan's dominant robotics/automotive supply base (NVIDIA, Sony) into a labor-constrained sector that automation has historically struggled to crack.

entities.desc: Japanese startup bridging conversational AI and service robotics. The dual competency in AI-driven customer conversation (ZEALS' original business) and physical robot deployment is a differentiated combination: most robotics companies lack the conversational AI layer, and most chatbot companies lack the physical execution layer. Part of Japan's broader service-robot ecosystem addressing the chronic labor shortage in hospitality and retail.

entities.desc: Honda is the only major automaker in this landscape with a 25-year humanoid robotics legacy (ASIMO, retired 2022; Asimo development formally continued as 'CL research' robots). **Honda Autonomous Work Vehicle (AWV):** Next-generation construction/industrial robot debuted 2024, replacing ASIMO's anthropomorphic form with a more utilitarian autonomous machine. **Honda 0 EV platform:** Honda's next-generation EV architecture emphasizing software-defined features and AI-driven ADAS. **Noetra consortium:** Honda is a founding investor alongside SoftBank, Sony, and NEC — contributing its multi-decade robotics hardware expertise and factory automation data. **GM AV partnership:** Honda's Cruise partnership (GM) for robotaxi commercialization entered a challenging restructuring phase when Cruise faced regulatory issues in 2023; Honda's AV strategy is in transition. **Joint ECU/software standardization with Nissan (#94, Aug 31, 2026):** Honda and Nissan concluded a joint development agreement to standardize core electronic control units (high-performance SoC-based HPCs and zone ECUs) plus the in-vehicle operating system, middleware, and vehicle control software underpinning next-generation software-defined vehicles (SDVs, ソフトウェア定義車両). The shared E/E architecture is targeted for both companies' next-gen SDVs from fiscal 2029, a narrower software-only successor to the 2024–25 merger talks that collapsed; rationale cited is faster development cycles and shared R&D cost against Chinese and US SDV competition.

entities.name: Nippon Steel
entities.desc: Japan's largest steelmaker, relevant to this landscape for two structural reasons. **High-strength steel for humanoid robots:** Nippon Steel's advanced high-strength steels (AHSS) and specialty alloys are feedstock for humanoid robot frames and precision actuator components — Nippon Steel has partnered with several humanoid startups to supply ultra-light, high-strength structural materials. **US Steel acquisition saga:** The blocked $14.9B US Steel acquisition (Biden Jan 2025 veto; contested under Trump) has become a case study in trade policy versus industrial policy in the AI/manufacturing era — the deal would have given Nippon Steel US domestic production for automotive AI supply chains. The outcome is still uncertain as of August 2026.

entities.name: Asahi Kasei
entities.desc: Japanese conglomerate with a critical semiconductor materials subsidiary: Asahi Kasei Microdevices (AKM), the world's leading producer of high-precision audio and industrial DAC/ADC chips. **AKM fab fire (2020) and rebuild:** AKM's primary chip fab burned down in October 2020 — the most disruptive single facility loss in the specialty chip market in a decade; recovery completed by 2023. AKM's precision analog chips are essential in AI inference hardware (high-precision signal conversion between the physical and digital world). Asahi Kasei's advanced battery separator materials are also used in EV and humanoid robot battery packs, making it a multi-point materials supplier to the AI hardware ecosystem.

entities.name: MUFG (Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group)
entities.desc: Japan's largest bank and primary institutional financier of the AI ecosystem. MUFG is a founding investor in Rapidus (as part of the eight-company consortium) — Japan's 2nm chip initiative. **AI deployment internally:** MUFG has deployed Anthropic Claude for internal document review, contract analysis, and regulatory compliance workflows across its global operations. **Stablecoin readiness:** MUFG is preparing for the 2026 Japanese stablecoin regulatory framework; digital yen/JPY-coin infrastructure may be co-developed with institutions like JPYC. MUFG's scale means its AI adoption decisions set industry norms across Japan's banking sector. **Canton Network JGB repo pilot (Aug 2026, cited Sept 15 in FSA priorities):** Four MUFG group companies (MUFG Bank, Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities, Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking, and MUFG itself) began testing Japanese government bond repo transactions on the Canton Network under the FSA's Payment Innovation Project, examining automated processing and 24-hour settlement. MUFG is also part of a joint MUFG/SMBC/Mizuho stablecoin framework targeted to go live before the end of Japan's fiscal 2026 (March 2027).

entities.name: SMBC (Sumitomo Mitsui Banking)

As Japan's stablecoin regulatory framework takes effect in 2026, SMBC is positioning as a custodian and settlement bank for JPY-denominated digital assets — potentially distributing JPYC and future MUFG/Mizuho stablecoin products.

entities.name: Bank of Japan (BOJ)
entities.desc: **September core CPI 2.1%, core-core 2.4% (#147, Oct 23, 2026):** National core CPI rose to 2.1% from 1.7%, in line with forecasts and the first reading above 2% in nine months; the ex-fresh-food-and-energy index rose to 2.4% from 1.9%, above the 2.3% forecast, with services at 1.5% from 1.2% and goods at 2.8%. Reuters sources expect no change at the Oct 29-30 meeting but a higher inflation forecast and possibly a statement that underlying inflation has probably reached 2%. Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said conditions for declaring an end to deflation have not yet been met. **Economists move the next hike to December (#146, Oct 22, 2026):** 83% of BOJ watchers in a Bloomberg survey expect a Dec 17-18 hike, none expect October, median terminal rate 1.75%. **Himino and Ueda close in on the 2% call (#141, #145, Oct 16-21, 2026):** Ueda said the October board will decide whether underlying inflation has reached 2% and that the bank will not let it rise further; Deputy Governor Himino said it is almost at 2% and that waiting has a cost. **Rate path in 2026:** raised the policy rate to 1.25% on Sept 18 on a 7-2 vote (dissenters Asada and Sato), its second hike in three months.

entities.name: Ministry of Finance (MoF)
entities.desc: **September trade: exports +16.7%, chips +49.4%, deficit ¥536.6bn (#145, Oct 21, 2026):** Customs data showed exports of ¥10.97tn, a 13th straight monthly rise but below the 20.1% consensus and August's 19.3%; imports rose 18.9% to ¥11.51tn and the deficit of ¥536.6bn was about three times the ¥181bn expected, though narrower than August's ¥1.11tn. Semiconductors and other electronic parts rose 49.4% to ¥933.7bn and electrical machinery 30.3% to ¥2.15tn; transport equipment rose 10.8%. Exports to the US rose 22.9% while imports from the US rose 44.8%; exports to China rose 8.6%. Mineral fuel imports rose 39.4% even with crude cargoes delayed by tankers rerouting around Bab el-Mandeb. **20-year JGB auction draws record 5.84x cover (#144, Oct 20, 2026):** bid-to-cover rose to 5.84 from 4.01 in September against a 3.73 12-month average, the highest on record; the 20-year yield fell as much as 6bp to 3.71%, lowest since Sept 9, and the 30-year fell about 5bp. Earlier in October the 20-year hit its highest since the mid-1990s and the 30-year a record. Fukoku Mutual said yields leave room to shift money from foreign bonds into JGBs. The same day the Fiscal System Council heard METI's ¥400bn Rapidus equity request. **Takaichi approval drops below 50% as food tax cut enters lower house (#142, Oct 17-18, 2026):** Kyodo poll put cabinet support at 49.1%, first sub-50% reading since October 2025, with more than 65% concerned about the food consumption tax cut (8% to 1% for two years from April 2027; with income-based cash benefits about ¥10tn over two years; cabinet approved Oct 9; target enactment by Dec 12). Funding source still unnamed; Takaichi rules out deficit-financing bonds. IMF Japan mission chief Rahul Anand called the temporary cut 'a very welcome step' but urged targeted, budget-neutral support and warned on debt-service costs. **Bessent skips Bangkok as the yen nears ¥160 (#136, Oct 9-12, 2026):** US Treasury Secretary Bessent will miss the IMF/World Bank meetings in Bangkok, removing a venue for a joint Katayama-Bessent yen message; Katayama and BOJ Governor Ueda attend. The yen posted a fourth weekly loss and traded ¥158.2-158.6 on Oct 12, with the US-Japan 10-year gap near 2.1 points (5.23% vs 3.09%). The July 31 joint intervention cost an estimated ¥8.45T near ¥164. **August current account: ¥4.06tn surplus on record primary income (#132, Oct 8, 2026):** MoF's preliminary balance of payments showed a ¥4.062tn surplus, well above the ¥3.19tn consensus and the 19th straight monthly surplus. Primary income hit a record ¥5.133tn (+21.6% y/y, highest since 1985 records), while the goods balance swung to a ¥687.7bn deficit and services posted a ¥115.8bn deficit. A weaker yen (down about 7.5% against the dollar y/y) inflated the yen value of overseas returns. **10-year auction draws strongest demand since May (#130, Oct 6, 2026):** The new 10-year JGB carried a 3.1% coupon (up from 2.7%); bid-to-cover was 3.76 versus 3.29 in September and a 12-month average of 3.21, and the tail narrowed to 0.02 from 0.12. The 10-year yield touched 3.115%, matching its highest since 1996, while the 20-year hit 3.99% and the 30-year held near its 4.235% record. A day earlier Takaichi told the Diet she would 'control' bond issuance. The 30-year auction follows on Oct 8. Japan's fiscal authority. Finance Minister: Satsuki Katayama (片山さつき). Authorized record ¥11.73T (~$74B) FX intervention (為替介入) April 28–May 27, 2026 — first since July 2024, surpassing prior monthly record. USD/JPY hit ¥155 then retraced to 159.3. Issued fresh verbal warnings June 2026. 300bp US-Japan rate gap drives structural yen carry trade pressure. **JGB new-issue coupon 2.7% (#33, Jul 2 2026):** MoF's auction of new 10-year JGB set coupon at 2.7% — highest new-issue coupon in 29 years. Auction described as soft (subscription ratio below prior levels), signaling JGB supply/demand tension as Takaichi's fiscal stance raises long-end vigilance. **Ambush FX intervention (#34, Jul 3–4 2026):** USD/JPY hit four-decade low near 162.8; roughly 1% yen surge occurred in holiday-thinned July 3–4 US trading — consistent with MoF's unannounced 'ambush' intervention tactics (not officially confirmed; MOF has declined to comment). Yen near 1986 lows entering Q3 2026. **Goldman 165 call (#38, Jul 8 2026):** Goldman Sachs cut 12-month USD/JPY forecast to 165 — among Wall Street's most bearish. Thesis: structural carry-trade pressure and US-Japan rate differential keep yen weak despite intervention risk. **GPIF head-fake (#41, Jul 11 2026):** Finance Minister Katayama said government will explore measures encouraging Japan's pension funds to substantially increase domestic asset holdings. Response was immediate: yen firmed toward 161, 10-year JGB yield pulled back from 30-year highs, Nikkei rose 1.2%. Described as a positioning squeeze (kuchisaki kainyū — verbal intervention) — GPIF formal allocation changes move through review processes, not press conferences. Concrete follow-up required to validate. **Intervention rally fades, current account surprise deficit (#72, Aug 10 2026):** The yen weakened as much as 1% to ¥159.35/$ on Aug 10 — the worst performer among G-10 currencies that day — erasing roughly half the gain from the Jul 31 US-Japan joint intervention (itself the first such coordinated action since 2011). MoF data released the same day showed Japan's current account unexpectedly swung to a ¥92.3bn deficit in June, adding a fundamentals-based headwind on top of the structural US-Japan rate differential. Katayama has repeated that authorities 'will not hesitate' to intervene again and disclosed plans to draw on the Fed's FIMA Repo Facility to extend intervention firepower without depleting FX reserves outright — a signal aimed at dispelling doubts about Japan's capacity for repeat action rather than a commitment to a specific defense level. **Intervention gains erode further, yen nears ¥160 (#73, Aug 11, 2026):** The yen weakened toward ¥159.4/$ on Aug 11 — Bloomberg reported it edging toward the 160 line for the first time since the Jul 31 joint US-Japan intervention — as traders test whether authorities will step in a third time. The Japan Times described the move as erasing roughly half of the intervention-driven bounce, compounding the Aug 10 current-account deficit surprise. With ¥160 historically treated as a psychological trigger level and Katayama's FIMA Repo Facility framing intended to signal firepower rather than commit to a specific defense line, the episode keeps intervention credibility — not the hold/hike decision itself — as the market's central near-term question heading into July CPI (Aug 21). **July trade data: exports fastest since Oct 2022, semiconductor equipment +49.1% (#83, Aug 20, 2026):** MoF's trade statistics showed exports up 23.2% YoY in July to ¥11.5T — beating the 19.9% consensus and the fastest pace since October 2022 — powered by a 49.1% jump in semiconductor-equipment shipment value tied to the global AI capex boom, alongside a weak yen (near 40-year lows against the dollar) that inflates yen-denominated export values. The composition matters: export volumes rose just 5.2%, meaning most of the headline gain reflects currency depreciation and higher selling prices rather than genuinely stronger shipment quantities — a reminder that a weak yen is flattering nominal trade figures even as the underlying real-demand picture is more modest. Imports rose faster still, +27.8% to a fresh record ¥12.1T, with petroleum imports up 87.8% on Hormuz-driven oil prices, widening the trade deficit to ¥634.5bn (a third consecutive monthly deficit, though narrower than the ¥680bn expected). Exports to China rose 25.8%, to the US 22%, to the EU 19.1% — broad-based, chip-and-auto-led strength across all three major markets. The data lands as one more upside-inflation data point (via import costs) reinforcing the BOJ's September rate-hike case, even as it flatters Japan's nominal trade headline. **JGB auctions become a global rates story, not just a domestic one (#91, Aug 24-27, 2026):** MoF's Aug 20 20-year JGB auction drew firmer-than-average demand even as the 20-year yield traded near its highest since 1996, and attention has now turned to two auctions in the coming week — 10-year notes on Sept 1 and 30-year bonds on Sept 3 — that Bloomberg and other outlets flagged as a potential trigger for renewed pressure on US Treasury yields. The mechanism: foreign investors now account for roughly 65% of monthly cash trading volume in Japan's government bond market (versus just 12% in 2009), so weak demand at a JGB auction reads as a global, not purely domestic, risk-appetite signal; conversely, rising JGB yields give Japan's own institutions — still holding over $1.1tn in US Treasuries — more reason to keep capital home rather than recycle it into US debt, a structural headwind for Treasury demand independent of Fed policy. With the 10-year JGB yield already near a three-decade high around 2.88-2.9% on BOJ hike expectations, the Sept 1 and Sept 3 auctions are shaping up as an early test of whether fiscal-concern-driven JGB weakness (Takaichi-era spending plans, a shrinking pool of domestic buyers) can now transmit directly into US long-end pricing — a channel institutional investors have historically discounted but which foreign-ownership concentration has made structurally more plausible in 2026. **Yen breaks ¥160, erasing more than half the July intervention gain (#92, Aug 28-29, 2026):** USD/JPY weakened past ¥160 for the first time since the Jul 31 joint US-Japan intervention, slipping as much as 0.5% to around ¥160.16 after incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to keep hitting the Fed's inflation target — a hawkish-on-inflation, dollar-supportive signal that widened the US-Japan rate differential further. ¥160 is the level markets and Tokyo officials have treated as the psychological/political intervention trigger since the Jul 31 action pushed the pair from ¥160 to ¥155; the retracement means the joint intervention has now given back more than half its gain in under a month. Katayama has not signaled a fresh intervention as of this writing, keeping the same open question live since Aug 10-11: whether authorities view a third action as necessary before the Sept 17-18 BOJ meeting, or whether they let a hawkish September hike do the work of supporting the currency instead. **Record ¥15.39tn confirmed spent on July-August intervention (#93, Aug 28-29, 2026):** MoF disclosed that Japan spent ¥15.39tn (~$96bn) on yen-buying, dollar-selling intervention between July 30 and Aug 26 — the largest monthly total on record, confirming the scale behind the Jul 31 joint US-Japan action. The disclosure lands the same week USD/JPY breached ¥160 again, retracing more than half that intervention's gain; 2026's cumulative intervention total now exceeds ¥27tn, already surpassing the prior full-year record of roughly ¥15tn set in 2024. The confirmed figure gives markets a hard number behind Katayama's repeated 'will not hesitate' rhetoric, but the fact that ¥15.39tn of firepower bought less than a month of yen support before ¥160 gave way again is itself the more market-relevant signal — reinforcing the view among some desks that rate policy, not intervention scale, will have to do more of the work from here. **G20 finance meeting: Bessent tells Japan to hike and end big stimulus (#99, Aug 31, 2026):** At the G20 finance ministers' meeting in Asheville, NC, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Japan it should accelerate BOJ rate hikes and abandon 'outdated ideas about big economic stimulus' — remarks read domestically as a direct challenge to PM Sanae Takaichi's expansionary fiscal approach, with Bessent reportedly suggesting Japan should instead 'sit back and enjoy the success of Abenomics and let that run.' Bessent separately told Reuters recent yen moves were 'not disorderly,' signaling little US appetite for a third joint intervention despite the record ¥15.39tn already spent in July-August — effectively pushing the policy burden back onto the BOJ's Sept 17-18 hike decision rather than further FX intervention. Japanese officials characterized the comments as Washington escalating its demands on Japanese fiscal and monetary policy simultaneously, adding a US-pressure dimension to the domestic hike debate ahead of the meeting. **Five-year JGB auction draws weakest demand in months (#102, Sept 9, 2026):** MoF's Sept 8 sale of five-year JGBs saw bid-to-cover fall to 3.42 (vs. 4.15 at the prior auction and a 3.44 12-month average) with a wider tail of 0.04 (vs. 0.02 prior) — the softest demand signal in months as investors turn cautious just over a week before the BOJ's Sept 17-18 meeting. The soft auction lands against persistent fiscal-supply concern under PM Takaichi's expansionary agenda: elevated government spending keeps JGB issuance high even as the pool of steady domestic buyers has structurally shrunk, the same dynamic flagged in the Aug 24-27 note on JGB auctions becoming a global, not just domestic, rates story. Separately, Takaichi economic adviser Takuji Aida — a reflationist historically skeptical of BOJ hikes — said he now expects a September hike followed by another by January, pulling forward his own prior forecast of a January 2027 move and adding to a sense of broadening consensus, even among fiscal doves, that further tightening is coming. **Cabinet reshuffle keeps Katayama, unfunded consumption-tax cut heads to parliament (#114, Sept 16-17, 2026):** PM Takaichi's first cabinet reshuffle retained Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and Economic Revitalization Minister Minoru Kiuchi, signaling continuity for the expansionary spending agenda already pressuring JGB issuance and auction demand in recent issues. The Cabinet adopted a two-year cut in the consumption tax on food from 8% to 1% plus household payouts, but without specifying financing — Takaichi has ruled out deficit-financing bonds while declining to detail an alternative funding path, a gap opposition lawmakers are expected to press when the Diet reconvenes in October. The reshuffle itself left markets largely unmoved (Nikkei flat, yen marginally firmer near ¥155.6, 10-year JGB slightly stronger), but an unfunded tax cut layered on top of already-strained fiscal metrics is a distinct medium-term risk to the same JGB-auction-demand and foreign-investor-share dynamics tracked above, independent of the BOJ's parallel rate-hike path. **August trade data: exports +19.3%, electronic components +52.3%, deficit widens to ¥1.1056tn (#116, Sept 16, 2026):** MoF's August trade statistics showed exports up 19.3% YoY to ¥10.05tn (beating the 18.4% consensus), the 12th consecutive month of export growth, led by a 52.3% surge in electronic-components shipments (including semiconductors) to ¥894.1bn — by far the fastest-growing major export line and a direct readout of the global AI capex cycle already lifting Tokyo Electron's and Kioxia's order books. Imports rose faster still, +28.0% to ¥11.15tn, pushing the trade balance to a ¥1.1056tn ($7.1bn) deficit — the fourth consecutive monthly deficit and the largest since January. The composition split is the read for positioning: semiconductor-linked export strength is a structural, AI-capex story that stands apart from the currency- and energy-driven deficit, and one shouldn't be read as a proxy for the other. **Markets reopen into live intervention watch (#117, Sept 24, 2026):** Tokyo's cash equity market reopened Sept 24 after a five-day Silver Week closure with the yen near ¥157-158/$, its softest level in months, and traders reporting authorities have already run rate checks -- a step that typically precedes intervention. The setup is unusual: the BOJ's Sept 18 rate hike to 1.25% would normally be currency-supportive, but a 7-2 dissenting vote left traders reading limited room for further hikes, so the yen kept weakening instead of stabilizing. That shifts the defense burden back onto MoF intervention, which cost a record ¥15.4tn in a single month earlier in 2026 for only a temporary effect. **Funding gap persists, 10Y JGB yield climbs toward 3%, Oct 5 extraordinary Diet convenes (#119, Sept 17-23, 2026):** The ¥5tn ($32bn)-a-year food consumption-tax cut approved in August still has no identified funding source; Finance Minister Katayama has pushed the decision to the FY2027 budget process due by late December. Of roughly 120 special tax measures expiring in FY2026, only three are expected to be abolished; a Foreign Exchange Fund Special Account surplus is already earmarked for defense spending; and the Japan Business Federation opposes the remaining obvious option, a corporate tax hike. The secondary-market 10-year JGB yield has climbed from roughly 1.6% to near 3% since the cut was floated, and FY2027 interest payments are now projected at ¥16.59tn -- up ¥3.5tn from FY2026. Takaichi said Sept 23 she is eager to pass the bill; an extraordinary Diet session convenes Oct 5, where the funding question will be the central fight, with Takaichi having already ruled out deficit-financing bonds to cover the gap. **Trump and Bessent back a stronger yen (#121, Sept 25, 2026):** Katayama disclosed that Trump raised concern about yen weakness at the Sept 22 Takaichi summit; Takaichi said an undervalued yen is a problem. Bessent said he and Katayama discussed 'the desirability of a strong yen that reflects Japan's strong economic fundamentals' and agreed to stay in close communication. USD/JPY eased from 158.60 to ~158; 10Y JGB touched 3.115%, a ~30-year high. **40-year JGB auction strongest since 2020 (#123, Sept 29, 2026):** bid-to-cover 3.1 vs 2.82 at the July sale and a 2.67 12-month average; 40-year yield about 4.23% and JGB futures rose after the result. Demand attributed to yields above 4% drawing life insurers back to the super-long end, a week after the 10-year JGB broke above 3% in a global bond selloff. 2-year auction Sept 30 with yields near 2%. **Food tax cut goes to the Diet as October food prices rise on 3,153 items (#128, Oct 5, 2026):** The extraordinary Diet opened Oct 5 with the bill to cut the consumption tax on food from 8% to 1% for two years from April 2027 at the center of debate; the roughly ¥5tn annual cost still has no named funding source. Teikoku Databank counted 3,153 food and drink price increases for October and 20,187 for 2026, a second straight year above 20,000.

entities.name: METI (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry)
entities.desc: **AI red team for national systems (#147, Oct 23, 2026):** Minister Ryosei Akazawa announced that IPA, the agency under METI, will set up a team in November that uses AI to run simulated attacks on Japanese systems and find weaknesses before criminals do; he said defenders must think like attackers. The announcement came as the PHP2Shell flaws, found by Wiz with AI models, pushed SoftBank, MUFG, Nomura, ANA, JR East and the Finance Ministry to take services offline. **¥400bn more Rapidus equity over FY2027-29 (#144, Oct 19, 2026):** told the Finance Ministry's Fiscal System Council it will request ¥150bn, ¥150bn and ¥100bn of industrial-investment equity for Rapidus, lifting cumulative state equity to ¥650bn so the company can borrow ¥2tn from banks. **Data center and cloud certification (#143, Nikkei Oct 19, 2026):** With MIC, plans a national security certification for data center operators and cloud providers in Japan, assessing business details, leak safeguards and equipment suppliers and building on IPA's JC-STAR label; finance and medical institutions would be told to use certified services (voluntary, from after FY2027), backed by an Economic Security Promotion Act amendment due in the January 2027 Diet session that adds prior notification and suspension orders. In practice expected to exclude Chinese providers. **TSMC Kumamoto 3nm approval (#143, Oct 16, 2026):** approved JASM's 3nm plan for Kumamoto Fab 2 (6,000 wafers/month by Dec 2028) and cut its subsidy cap to ¥645.15B, with more to be requested in the FY2027 budget. **Critical-minerals certification for Kyocera tungsten recycling (#135, Oct 9, 2026):** certified Kyocera's plan to recover tungsten carbide from used tools at its Kagoshima Sendai plant from FY2030 under the critical-minerals supply-security program, with a ¥3B subsidy, after Chinese tungsten carbide shipments to Japan fell to zero Feb-Apr 2026. **AI regulation call and power-chip realignment (#130, Oct 2, 2026):** Minister Ryosei Akazawa announced, with the Digital Agency and Cabinet Office, a call (Oct 19-30) for laws, ordinances, notices and circulars that block deployment of LLMs, AI agents and physical AI such as AI robots, fully driverless vehicles and AI drones; METI will give hands-on support using the Industrial Competitiveness Enhancement Act's regulatory tools. At the same briefing he declined to comment on the stalled Rohm-Toshiba-Mitsubishi Electric power-chip merger but said METI will back domestic collaboration and realignment in power semiconductors. Japan's industrial policy ministry. Core AI infrastructure funder and semiconductor strategist. ¥1.23T AI/semiconductor budget envelope; ¥387.3B specifically for AI development. Backs Rapidus 2nm semiconductor project (~¥2.35T total government commitment). AI Promotion Act (AI推進法): enacted 2026, innovation-first, voluntary guidelines for most applications. **Genesis Mission (Issue #11, Jun 4–5, 2026):** Japan named first international partner in U.S. DOE Genesis Mission — $1B combined ($500M each) over 5 years; 12 U.S. national labs + 12 Japanese research institutions; quantum technology, nuclear fusion, biotechnology, materials AI, advanced manufacturing. MEXT co-sponsoring. **AI Basic Plan revision (Issue #22, Jun 20, 2026):** Draft revision released for public comment — adds enhanced international cooperation provisions and new cybersecurity plank on AI-enabled cyberattacks. Cabinet approval sought at early date; cybersecurity budget line likely to follow. **Noetra / ¥387.3B commitment (#31):** Largest single domestic AI commitment in Japan's history; ¥300B separately allocated to AI foundation models in FY2026 budget; Noetra's ¥387.3B exceeds prior NEDO AI programs by several multiples. **Revised AI Robotics Strategy (#32, Jul 1 2026):** 10 million AI-equipped robots across 18 sectors by 2040; gated on Noetra model readiness. **FSA AI compliance (#24):** Joint finalization of AI workflow guidelines effective July 1, 2026. **VTLA Dataset Consortium (#33, Jul 2 2026):** METI/NEDO solicitation selected Kawasaki+Fanuc+Yaskawa+Osaka University+FingerVision consortium to build VTLA physical-AI dataset — up to ¥2B over Aug 2026–Jul 2027. Goal: 5,000 hours of video, tactile, and motion data from automotive, robotics, and food-production sites; first multi-vendor standardized physical-AI training corpus in Japan. **Micron Hiroshima subsidy (#35, Jul 4 2026):** METI underwrote up to ¥536B of Micron's ¥1.5T Hiroshima HBM fab (groundbreaking Jul 4). Largest single semiconductor subsidy Japan has authorized; targets HBM supply for AI accelerators. **Japan AX / Second AI Basic Plan (#42, Jul 10 2026):** Prime Minister Takaichi's AI Strategy Headquarters adopted second-phase AI Basic Plan. Brands agenda "Japan AX" (日本AX). Two pillars: vertical AI (sector-specific models) + physical AI. 19 priority fields sorted by marketability, public value, and strategic importance. Orders cross-ministerial regulatory rewrite assuming AI is in the loop. AISI expanded to use frontier models for safety evaluation and cyber defense. Test: late-August FY2027 budget requests — dated line items per priority field determine whether plan has teeth. **Tower Semiconductor grant (#45, Jul 14 2026):** ~$1B in Japanese government grants supporting Tower's $3B silicon photonics + silicon-germanium expansion at Arai facility (300mm conversion). **¥370T economic-security investment blueprint (#81, Aug 11 2026):** The Takaichi Cabinet's long-term economic and fiscal policy guidelines target ¥370T ($2.3T) in combined public-private investment across 17 strategic sectors through fiscal 2040, with semiconductors and AI as the centerpiece alongside quantum, energy, biotech, and content. Sector detail includes ¥32.7T for data centers and storage batteries by FY2035. Unlike predecessor Ishiba's guidelines, the blueprint drops explicit 'fiscal consolidation' language in favor of 'stably' reducing the debt-to-GDP ratio over time. Ahead of the announcement, executives from Anthropic, TSMC, Microsoft, and Oracle met with the Takaichi government to make investment pitches — foreign frontier-AI and chip capacity now actively courting Japan's 17-sector spending envelope rather than the reverse. **Record ¥7.7T FY2027 budget request filed (#97, Sept 1, 2026):** METI submitted its fiscal 2027 budget request to the Finance Ministry on the Sept 1 government-wide deadline, seeking ¥7.7268 trillion — roughly 2.5x the prior year's request — with ¥4.525T of that under a new no-preset-ceiling investment quota and approximately ¥1.4T earmarked specifically for AI, semiconductor, and robotics initiatives. The request folds in the additional ¥150bn capital injection for Rapidus first flagged Aug 21, now a formal line item. METI's ask is one piece of a government-wide FY2027 budget request total approaching ¥130T across all ministries — a fourth consecutive record high — which the Finance Ministry will review ahead of Cabinet approval by year-end. The scale of the request is the clearest budget-cycle evidence yet of how far the Aug 11 ¥370T/17-sector economic-security blueprint has been translated into ministry-level spending asks. **$550B US investment pact: AI/chips to headline next tranche (#100, Sept 4, 2026):** Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa told reporters in Washington that AI and semiconductor projects will carry 'very significant weight' in the next funding round of the Japan-US $550B investment framework, following meetings with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and USTR Jamieson Greer. Only $109B of the $550B has been committed after more than a year — $36B into US oil, gas, and mineral projects and $73B into a nuclear project spanning Tennessee/Alabama plus gas plants in Pennsylvania/Texas — and none of it into AI or chips yet. Akazawa declined to detail the third tranche. The structure caps direct equity at just 1-2% of the total, with the remainder as loans and guarantees through Japan's state-backed lenders (JBIC, NEXI) — meaning any AI/chip allocation would flow mostly as government-backed financing for US-based capacity rather than direct investment, a distinct channel from METI's domestic Rapidus/Kioxia subsidy programs tracked above. **HR development ecosystem project: Tokyo Electron selected for India training center (#114, Sept 19-20, 2026):** METI has selected Tokyo Electron to build a semiconductor HR-development-ecosystem hub in India, under which TEL will open a training center in Gujarat in 2027 to build a fab-engineer pipeline alongside local businesses and educational institutions. It's METI's workforce-side complement to its capital-heavy subsidy programs (Rapidus, Micron Hiroshima, Tower Semiconductor) — extending Japan's equipment-and-materials industrial-policy reach into human-capital formation for a foreign market, rather than only funding domestic capacity.

entities.name: Ministry of Justice (MOJ)
entities.desc: Japan's justice ministry. **Voice-rights interpretive guidance (#71, Aug 7, 2026):** Published a report — the output of a five-session expert study group running since April 2026 — stating that an individual's voice is already protected under existing Japanese law even without a dedicated statute: publicity rights (パブリシティー権, the exclusive right to commercially exploit the customer-drawing power of one's name or likeness) and personality-rights-derived protection against unwanted use (the 'right not to be used without cause,' みだりに利用されない権利) both extend to voice. Concretely, the MOJ said posting an unauthorized AI-cloned cover version of a singer's or voice actor's voice on social media for profit (AIカバー, 'AI cover') can constitute a publicity-rights violation — though ordinary human impressions or mimicry generally do not infringe. The guidance follows a wave of voice-actor complaints since AI voice-cloning tools proliferated from around 2023, including a lawsuit filed by voice actor Kenjiro Tsuda in November 2025 against a video-platform operator over an unauthorized AI-cloned video of his voice. No dedicated 'voice rights' statute yet exists — the report is interpretive guidance, not new legislation — but it gives claimants a clearer legal theory and puts platforms and AI voice-synthesis services on notice ahead of any future codification.

Implementation period August 2026 – July 2027. The arrangement — three direct competitors agreeing to share factory floor data under a government mandate — is designed to give Japan's physical AI model (Noetra) training data advantages comparable to China's state-directed data pooling. **Other major bets:** ¥1tn Noetra foundation-model program; Hitachi–Intel–AIST silicon spin-qubit project (through March 2029).
