Targets US$10bn IPO path within 5 years
Competes vs. Nissan-Wayve-Uber Tokyo robotaxi pilot

entities.bio: Founded 2021, Tokyo, by CEO Issei Yamamoto. Private; backed by Denso, MUFG Bank, AMD Ventures, Mitsubishi Corporation, Super Micro Computer, and Tokyo Electron Device. Develops end-to-end deep-learning autonomous driving software for driver-assistance and robotaxi applications, targeting Japan and the US.

entities.name: Samsung Electronics (Japan Packaging)
entities.zh: サムスン電子（日本パッケージング）
entities.desc: South Korea's Samsung Electronics is deepening its footprint in Japan's back-end (advanced packaging) supply chain rather than front-end fabrication, betting that Japan's strength in packaging materials — not logic nodes — is the next axis of AI-chip competition. **Advanced Package Lab (APL) opens in Yokohama (#109, Sept 8, 2026):** Samsung held an opening ceremony for its APL in the Minato Mirai district — a ~6,600 sqm facility with a clean room for evaluating back-end materials and prototyping under real production conditions. Total investment is ¥40bn ($277M), of which Japan's METI is funding ¥22.5bn (over half), plus a ¥2.5bn subsidy from the City of Yokohama. Ninety-five South Korean and Japanese researchers will work on packaging technology for HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) and GPU integration — the back-end steps that connect multiple chips together and are emerging as a new competitive axis as front-end circuit miniaturization approaches physical limits. **Supply-chain significance:** Samsung already works with 50+ Japanese companies on AI-chip back-end processes; Japan holds outsized share in packaging materials (Sumitomo Bakelite ~40% of global encapsulation materials; Resonac and Mitsubishi Gas Chemical lead in substrate materials). Fifteen major Japanese chip firms, including Tokyo Electron and Ibiden, attended the opening — a direct read-through for TEL's equipment-and-materials revenue base distinct from its TSMC/JASM exposure. The Yokohama base lets Samsung evaluate and prototype with Japanese materials locally before porting only validated technologies to Korean mass-production lines, and is explicitly framed as competing with TSMC (#1 in advanced packaging) and SK Hynix (HBM leader) by tightening Samsung's own back-end supply chain.

tags.l: APL opens Yokohama, ¥40bn total, METI funds >half (Sept 8)
50+ Japanese back-end partners; TEL, Ibiden attended opening
Competes vs. TSMC (packaging #1) and SK Hynix (HBM #1)

entities.bio: Samsung Electronics (founded 1969, Suwon, South Korea; listed Korea Exchange 005930) is the world's largest memory-chip maker. This entry tracks its Japan-based advanced-packaging R&D operations, distinct from its Korean fabs — a strategic bet on Japanese back-end materials expertise (encapsulation, substrates) to strengthen its position in AI-chip packaging against TSMC and SK Hynix.

entities.name: GlobalFoundries
entities.zh: グローバルファウンドリーズ
entities.bio: US-headquartered contract chipmaker (foundry) spun off from AMD's manufacturing operations in 2009, listed on Nasdaq since 2021. Focuses on specialty and logic semiconductor manufacturing rather than leading-edge process nodes.
entities.desc: **Selected to run Japan-funded New York fabs (#138, Oct 14, 2026):** Japan will put up to about $21bn into as many as two fabs in Malta, New York, under its $550bn investment pledge to Washington, with GlobalFoundries operating them for fees over at least 20 years. The first fab starts construction in 2026, targets output in 2029 and about 900,000 300mm wafers a year; a decision on the second comes before the end of 2028. Renesas and Apple are named initial customers. Japan supplies the capital, cash flows split evenly until a set threshold and then 90% to the US, and the US stake in GlobalFoundries rises from 3% to 7%. CEO Tim Breen wants Japanese tool makers such as Tokyo Electron in the build. Shares rose more than 4%. **Background (#112, Sept 2026):** Working-level Japan-US talks on a ¥2-3tn logic fab, the first chip project in the tariff deal, were held Sept 14-15.

tags.l: 90% of later cash flow to US

entities.name: THK Corporation
entities.bio: Founded 1971, Tokyo. Global leader in linear motion (LM) guide systems for machine tools and robotics. Listed TSE (6481). Core business supplies precision motion components used across the robotics and factory-automation industry.
entities.desc: Demonstrated a teleoperated robot at Tokyo's Physical AI Summit (Sept 16, 2026) that picks up bottles, bags and boxes and can hammer a nail into wood using articulated arms and grippers, showcasing precision manipulation built on THK's own linear-motion component expertise.

entities.name: ugo
entities.bio: Japanese robotics venture developing semi-humanoid robots for remote operation and physical-AI data collection. Core product: the ugo Nova platform.
entities.desc: Demonstrated its ugo Nova semi-humanoid performing a teleoperated drilling task at Tokyo's Physical AI Summit (Sept 16, 2026). ugo Nova uses two seven-axis arms plus additional head and waist joints, and is designed to collect real-world manipulation data that feeds back into training ugo's own physical-AI models — a hardware-first approach to building physical AI capability.

tags.l: Data-collection strategy for physical AI training

entities.name: Fujifilm
entities.bio: Founded 1934, Tokyo. Diversified imaging, materials, and healthcare conglomerate. Listed TSE (4901). Semiconductor-materials business supplies process chemicals and high-purity materials to global chipmakers.
entities.desc: Announced a ₹800 crore ($83M) investment in a new semiconductor-materials plant in India (Semicon India 2026, Sept 19), targeting front-end process chemicals in Phase 1 (construction FY2026, production FY2028) and surface-conditioning/high-purity chemicals in Phase 2. Signed an MoU with Tata Electronics to supply materials for Tata's Dholera, Gujarat fab.

entities.name: Sumitomo Chemical
entities.bio: Founded 1913, Tokyo. Major Japanese chemicals conglomerate spanning petrochemicals, materials, and semiconductor-grade chemicals. Listed TSE (4005).
entities.desc: Signed an MoU with Tata Electronics (Sept 2026) to supply semiconductor materials — photoresists and high-purity chemicals including hydrogen peroxide, isopropyl alcohol, ammonia water, and sulfuric acid — for Tata's upcoming Dholera, Gujarat fab, and will explore local manufacturing of these materials in India.

entities.name: Hirata Corporation
entities.bio: Founded 1951, Kumamoto. Japanese automation and material-handling equipment maker serving semiconductor, display, and automotive manufacturing. Listed TSE (6258).
entities.desc: Bringing its semiconductor automation and material-handling portfolio into India through subsidiary ATS India (announced Sept 2026) — Equipment Front End Modules (EFEM), FOPLP load ports, panel-handling robots, and high-performance wafer-handling robots used in fabrication and advanced packaging.

entities.name: Preferred Computing Infrastructure (PFCI)
entities.zh: プリファードコンピューティングインフラストラクチャー
entities.bio: Founded 2025 in Tokyo as a Preferred Networks (PFN) Group company. Builds and operates high-efficiency AI computing infrastructure powered primarily by PFN's MN-Core series accelerators, delivered as the Preferred Computing Platform (PFCP) AI cloud service.
entities.desc: PFN's dedicated AI-cloud vehicle, standing up compute infrastructure around PFN's proprietary MN-Core chips rather than third-party GPUs. **MN-Core 2 for Matlantis (#116, Sept 18, 2026):** PFCI and PFN announced PFCP will offer MN-Core 2 as a selectable compute resource for Matlantis, PFN's commercial materials-discovery simulator — PFCI's first prominent public role in bringing an in-house PFN Group product to an external paying customer base via MN-Core-powered cloud compute.

tags.l: MN-Core 2 for Matlantis via PFCP cloud platform (Sept 18)

entities.name: CADDi
entities.bio: Founded in 2017 by Yusaku Kato and Kenta Suenaga, CADDi builds AI software that reads manufacturers' engineering drawings and structures the data locked inside them. Its original product, CADDi Drawer (2022), let engineers search archived part designs by shape or specification rather than by filename; the platform has since broadened into what the company calls an AI data platform for manufacturing, pulling together CAD files, ERP records, and other factory-floor data sources. Backed by Atomico, Globis Capital Partners, and Japan Post Asset Management prior to its Series D.
entities.desc: **$114mn Series D at $1.2bn valuation, unicorn status (#117, Sept 24, 2026):** CADDi raised ¥17.7bn ($114mn) on Sept 16, lifting its valuation to ¥182bn ($1.2bn) and crossing into unicorn territory. New investors Moore Strategic Ventures, Coreline Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and Toyota's Woven Capital joined returning backers Atomico, Globis Capital Partners, and Japan Post Asset Management, taking total funding to $234mn. Proceeds are earmarked for proprietary AI development and North American expansion, where manufacturers face the same drawing-search problem CADDi solved domestically but with far less existing AI tooling built for factory-floor use.

tags.l: Toyota's Woven Capital joins as new investor

entities.name: Panasonic Energy
entities.zh: パナソニックエナジー
entities.bio: Panasonic Energy is the battery subsidiary of Panasonic Holdings, a longtime lithium-ion cell supplier to Tesla and other automakers. The unit has been expanding beyond automotive cells into data-center and next-generation battery chemistries as EV demand growth has slowed relative to earlier forecasts.
entities.desc: **Opens 500-person battery R&D hub, targets 2x development efficiency by FY2031 (#117, Sept 24, 2026):** Panasonic Energy opened Energy Innovation Square in Kadoma, Osaka on Sept 16 -- a lithium-ion battery R&D facility staffed by roughly 500 researchers covering materials development, cell design, and prototyping under one roof. Combined with the adjacent Suminoe production-development site (about 800 staff total), it forms one of Japan's largest dedicated battery-development clusters. Panasonic named automotive and data-center batteries as its immediate priority, with drones, robotaxis, and humanoid robots flagged as future demand categories rather than markets it is building capacity against today.

tags.l: Energy Innovation Square opens in Kadoma, Osaka (Sept 16)
Robotics/robotaxi batteries named as future, not current, priority

entities.name: EdgeCortix
entities.zh: エッジコーティックス
entities.bio: Founded 2019 in Tokyo by Sakyasingha Dasgupta, a former AI researcher, EdgeCortix designs energy-efficient AI accelerators for edge and robotics workloads. Its products include the SAKURA-II edge AI chip, the runtime-reconfigurable DNA-X accelerator architecture and the MERA software stack. Privately held.
entities.desc: **RAIDEN physical-AI chiplet platform (#120, Sept 24, 2026):** Launched a scalable chiplet family; the four-die RAIDEN-X4 delivers up to 3.36 PFLOPS FP4, 256 GB memory and 1.54 TB/s die-to-die bandwidth (~1.6x Jetson AGX Thor per MONOist). Kawasaki Heavy Industries selected it for aerospace and defense products and Unigen is building servers. Sampling early 2027, volume 2H 2027; foundry, node and pricing undisclosed.

entities.name: Nippon Life Insurance
entities.bio: Japan's largest life insurer, founded 1889 in Osaka as a mutual company. One of the largest institutional holders of JGBs and foreign bonds, and an expanding lender to infrastructure and AI data center projects.
entities.desc: **AI data center lender under FSA review (#120, Sept 25, 2026):** About ¥1 trillion of AI infrastructure loans outstanding as of March 2026, with a ¥2 trillion target by 2035 at project-finance spreads above 2 points; lending mainly to US hyperscaler projects including Amazon. Plans a dedicated screening team next year as the FSA steps up scrutiny.

tags.l: FSA review of US data center loans

entities.name: Mitsubishi Chemical Group
entities.zh: 三菱ケミカルグループ
entities.bio: Japan's largest chemical group, formed through the 2017 merger of Mitsubishi Chemical, Mitsubishi Plastics and Mitsubishi Rayon under the Mitsubishi Chemical Holdings umbrella (renamed Mitsubishi Chemical Group in 2022), headquartered in Tokyo. Its semiconductor exposure runs through specialty materials, including gallium nitride (GaN) single-crystal substrates produced at its Tsukuba site in Ibaraki. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: **6-inch GaN substrates for power chips (#121, Sept 24, 2026):** Mitsubishi Chemical will ship 6-inch gallium nitride substrate samples for power semiconductors to customers by March 2027, targeting AI data center power conversion and EV/autonomous drivetrains. 4-inch substrates are in mass production at Tsukuba (mainly for projector lasers) and under customer evaluation for power devices; a GaN single-crystal pilot line with Japan Steel Works in Muroran, Hokkaido is preparing 6-inch samples, and 8-inch is in development. CTO Masaru Utsunomiya said late entrants struggle once the supply window closes; the company is weighing location and timing for large-diameter capacity.

tags.l: Pilot line with Japan Steel Works, Muroran
No capex or device partner announced yet

entities.name: Sakai Chemical Industry
entities.bio: Founded 1918 in Sakai, Osaka, from a zinc oxide business whose early products included white face powder (oshiroi) used in traditional makeup. Makes titanium dioxide, zinc and barium compounds, cosmetic and pharmaceutical materials, and electronic materials. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: One of a handful of merchant suppliers of hydrothermally synthesized barium titanate (チタン酸バリウム), the fine dielectric powder stacked inside multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs); Murata makes much of its own powder in-house. **AI-server capacitor bottleneck (#122, Bloomberg Sept 27 / Japan Times Sept 28, 2026):** Bloomberg reported that capacity for its capacitor raw materials is filling quickly as AI servers, which carry far more MLCCs per rack than conventional servers, pull demand upstream. Electronic materials are a minority of group sales next to titanium dioxide, cosmetic and pharmaceutical materials, so pricing and new capacity decide how much of the AI demand reaches earnings. **Peer expansion:** Nippon Chemical Industrial said Aug 18, 2026 it will raise barium titanate capacity about 1.5x in FY2027 for AI-server MLCCs; on Sept 28 Sakai announced its exit from pharmacopoeia-grade barium sulfate.

tags.l: Peer Nippon Chemical adding 1.5x capacity FY2027
Electronic materials a minority of sales

entities.name: SAIMEMORY
entities.bio: Established December 2024 and launched in June 2025 as a SoftBank subsidiary, with the University of Tokyo as a research partner; CEO Hideya Yamaguchi. Develops Z-Angle Memory (ZAM), a stacked DRAM for AI built on Intel's Next Generation DRAM Bonding work under a partnership formalized in February 2026. Series A funding included SoftBank, Fujitsu, the Development Bank of Japan and RIKEN; the program also receives NEDO support.
entities.desc: SoftBank's attempt to put Japan back into advanced DRAM with an alternative to HBM. **Shinko Electric packaging deal (#123, Sept 28, 2026):** basic agreement with Shinko Electric Industries to co-develop the packaging, assembly and manufacturing processes for ZAM, which stands DRAM dies upright side by side (versus HBM's flat stack, heat-limited at about 20 layers) and links them with magnetically coupled wireless I/O. Targets: prototypes in FY2027, practical use in FY2029. **VLSI Symposium demo with Intel (#15, June 2026):** ZAM-based HB3DM design claimed roughly 40% lower power than conventional HBM; up to 512GB per chip targeted.

tags.l: Unproven at volume; HBM incumbents moving fast

entities.name: Shinko Electric Industries
entities.bio: Founded 1946 in Nagano. Maker of flip-chip package substrates, lead frames and electrostatic chucks for high-end processors and chipmaking equipment. Formerly a listed Fujitsu subsidiary; taken private in 2025 by a consortium led by the state-backed Japan Investment Corporation with Dai Nippon Printing and Mitsui Chemicals.
entities.desc: One of Japan's key advanced-packaging substrate suppliers for AI processors. **Buys JDI's Mobara plant for FC-BGA expansion (#126, Sept 30, 2026):** agreed to acquire Japan Display's idle 373,000 m² Mobara LCD plant in Chiba as a new core plant for flip-chip (FC-BGA) substrates used in AI accelerators and data center chips; the western ~233,000 m² goes to supplier FICT for circuit boards. Transfer end-March 2027, production from FY2028; price undisclosed, JDI books a ¥51.4B gain. Shinko said Nagano sites lack room for the larger, higher-layer substrates AI chips need. **ZAM packaging partner for SAIMEMORY (#123, Sept 28, 2026):** basic agreement to develop packaging and high-density assembly for SoftBank-backed SAIMEMORY's Z-Angle Memory, targeting practical use in FY2029.

tags.l: Buys JDI Mobara plant for FC-BGA (Sept 30)
New capacity arrives after current crunch

entities.name: TDK Corporation
entities.bio: Founded in 1935 in Tokyo by Kenzo Saito to commercialize ferrite, a magnetic material invented at Tokyo Institute of Technology. Now a diversified electronic-components maker spanning multilayer ceramic capacitors, inductors, sensors, and lithium-ion battery cells for phones and devices. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: One of Japan's four large passive-component makers, with a battery business that gives it exposure to consumer devices and power storage. **MOU with Taiyo Yuden on AI-grade components (#124, Sept 29, 2026):** TDK and Taiyo Yuden signed a memorandum of understanding to explore joint development of high-capacitance MLCCs and inductors for AI data centers, servers and physical AI, plus cooperation in manufacturing and procurement, and will consider a capital alliance. The partners may seek joint METI approval under the Economic Security Promotion Act. TDK shares rose about 1.3-2.5% on Sept 30 while Murata fell 2.7%.

tags.l: AI server MLCC and inductor demand
No terms or timeline; integration risk

entities.name: Taiyo Yuden
entities.bio: Founded in 1950 in Tokyo by Kenji Sato as a maker of ceramic capacitors. Specializes in multilayer ceramic capacitors, inductors and high-frequency modules for smartphones, autos and servers. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime market.
entities.desc: A pure-play passive-component maker whose earnings track MLCC pricing and the AI server build. **MOU with TDK on AI-grade components (#124, Sept 29, 2026):** agreed with TDK to explore joint development of high-capacitance, high-reliability MLCCs and inductors for AI data centers and physical AI, cooperation in manufacturing and procurement, and a possible capital alliance. Shares rose about 2.8-3.8% on Sept 30. The combination would pair the third- and fourth-largest MLCC makers against Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and fast-growing Chinese suppliers.

tags.l: MLCC supply tight on AI servers

entities.name: JERA
entities.bio: Founded 2015 in Tokyo as a 50-50 joint venture of TEPCO (Tokyo Electric Power) and Chubu Electric Power, which merged their fuel procurement and thermal generation into it. Japan's largest power generator, producing roughly a third of the country's electricity, mostly from LNG-fired plants. Unlisted; exposure runs through its two listed parents.
entities.desc: **Power-plant AI data center model (#126, Oct 1, 2026):** signed an MOU with Dell Technologies and UK developer RHAELM to build a 400 MW, $15B+ AI data center beside its gas-fired Chiba thermal plant, with Apollo financing; JERA supplies land and 400 MW for 15-25 years, RHAELM builds and operates, Dell provides rack-scale AI servers. First operations 2028, full capacity 2029. The partners target several gigawatts at other JERA plants in the 2030s (FT: ~$140B full rollout). On-site power avoids grid-connection queues around Tokyo.

tags.l: Multi-GW plan across JERA plants in 2030s
No tenant named; LNG cost exposure

entities.name: Japan Display Inc. (JDI)
entities.zh: ジャパンディスプレイ
entities.bio: Formed in 2012 in Tokyo by merging the small and mid-size LCD units of Sony, Toshiba and Hitachi with backing from the state-backed Innovation Network Corporation of Japan. Maker of LCD and OLED panels for phones, cars and wearables. Listed on the TSE Prime market since 2014; later rescued by Ichigo Asset Management.
entities.desc: **Sells Mobara plant to Shinko Electric (#126, Sept 30, 2026):** agreed to sell its idle Mobara (Chiba) LCD plant, shut in November 2025, to Shinko Electric for advanced AI-chip substrates; transfer end-March 2027, with a ¥51.4B extraordinary gain in FY to March 2027. Micron had reportedly studied the site and JDI had floated a 100 MW data center there. **Restructuring:** ¥78.2B operating loss in FY to March 2025; sold Tottori plant March 2026 and is consolidating at Ishikawa. Its idle fabs are becoming supply for Japan's chip back-end and AI infrastructure buildout.

tags.l: Idle LCD fabs repurposed for AI chips

entities.name: ELYZA
entities.bio: Founded 2018 in Tokyo by alumni of Professor Yutaka Matsuo's lab at the University of Tokyo; CEO Yuya Soneoka. Builds Japanese-language LLMs and enterprise generative-AI products. KDDI took a controlling stake in 2024 and consolidates it as a subsidiary.
entities.desc: **Reasoning models on Japan's public base model (#128, Oct 2, 2026):** Released ELYZA-Thinking-1.0 in 33B dense and 32B-A3B mixture-of-experts versions under Apache 2.0, post-trained on NII's LLM-jp-4 with Japanese-translated math and code, several million synthetic reasoning examples (about half in Japanese) and reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks. The 33B model averages 61.7 on ELYZA's 20-benchmark suite, above NII's own LLM-jp-4.1 thinking model (60.6) and Qwen3-32B (58.1), below Qwen3.5-27B (68.2) and Gemma 4 31B (70.5). **ELYZA RSI Research:** A new unit for recursive self-improvement; ELYZA says agents handled most of the training and evaluation, with 1-2 person-days of human work per model, and describes this as groundwork rather than RSI itself. It also walked back an English 'fully domestic' claim. **Earlier:** Its Llama-based Japanese models claimed GPT-4-level Japanese scores in 2024, the result that preceded KDDI's investment.

tags.l: ELYZA RSI Research: agent-run model development

entities.name: National Institute of Informatics (NII)
entities.desc: Inter-university research institute in Tokyo that runs the LLM-jp project and its Research and Development Center for Large Language Models, Japan's main public effort to pre-train open LLMs from scratch. **LLM-jp-4.1 (#128, Sept 28, 2026):** Released 8B, 33B and 32B-A3B models with tool calling and stronger STEM results, trained on 11.7 trillion tokens, Apache 2.0, with SFT and DPO data published alongside. The 33B thinking model scored 7.76 on Japanese MT-Bench versus 7.29 for GPT-4o. **Downstream use:** KDDI's ELYZA built its ELYZA-Thinking-1.0 reasoning models on LLM-jp-4 within days, the first large commercial adoption of the public base model.

entities.name: Air Liquide Japan
entities.bio: Japanese arm of Paris-based industrial gas group Air Liquide (founded 1902), active in Japan's electronics sector for more than 40 years. Runs about 78 facilities in Japan and an advanced materials center in Tsukuba. Competes with Nippon Sanso Holdings (TSE: 4091) for on-site gas supply to chip fabs.
entities.desc: **€170M+ for a Kyushu logic fab (#128, Sept 30, 2026):** Will build, own and operate several ultra-high-purity gas units (nitrogen, oxygen, argon, hydrogen) plus large backup storage for an unnamed leading chipmaker's logic expansion in southern Japan, under a long-term supply contract. The profile matches TSMC JASM's 3nm second fab in Kumamoto. **€200M for Hiroshima (Apr 16, 2026):** Two units supplying ultra-pure nitrogen, oxygen and argon to a major chipmaker in Hiroshima, starting by end-2028. Together the two awards put about €370M of on-site gas capacity behind Japan's AI-chip buildout this year.

entities.name: Rohm
entities.bio: Founded in 1958 in Kyoto by Kenichiro Sato as a resistor maker (Toyo Denshi Kogyo) and renamed Rohm in 1981. Today a Kyoto-based maker of power and analog chips, with silicon carbide (SiC) as its growth bet after the 2009 acquisition of Germany's SiCrystal. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
entities.desc: **Power-chip merger talks stall (#130, Sept 30-Oct 2, 2026):** Rohm, Toshiba's device unit and Mitsubishi Electric signed a basic agreement on March 27, 2026 to integrate their power-semiconductor businesses, most likely under a holding company. Jiji reported on Sept 30 that the summer target has slipped because the three cannot agree on equity ratios, the scope of carved-out businesses and who leads; the new goal is the November interim results, with March 2027 as a fallback, and Chinese antitrust clearance is required. Combined, the group would rank second globally behind Infineon. METI minister Akazawa said on Oct 2 he would back domestic realignment. **Denso bid withdrawn (Apr 28, 2026):** Denso dropped its proposal to take a stake in Rohm after failing to secure board support, which cleared the way for the three-way talks. **SiC overhang:** Rohm's heavy SiC capex has met weak EV demand, the main reason it needs scale partners.

tags.l: 3-way power-chip merger talks slip to Nov or Mar 2027

entities.name: Goodman Group
entities.zh: グッドマン・グループ
entities.bio: Founded 1989 in Sydney by Greg Goodman as an industrial property developer; listed on the ASX and now Australia's largest property company by market value. It develops and manages logistics and industrial estates across Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Americas and has turned much of its development pipeline toward powered data center sites. Operates in Japan through Goodman Japan, a long-standing logistics warehouse developer around Greater Tokyo and Osaka.
entities.desc: **Tsukuba backlash (#131, Oct 7, 2026):** Goodman's planned 1 GW, roughly ¥3 trillion ($20bn) data center campus on a 45-hectare site in Tsukuba's Oho district, Ibaraki, one of the largest foreign-backed digital infrastructure projects in Japan, faces organised local opposition. The first 50 MW phase began construction earlier in 2026 next to housing, a hospital and a nursing home. Residents say 2023 filings described a logistics warehouse; about 800 have signed for a public town hall and threaten protests, while Goodman's only sessions so far were invitation-only dinners in August. Goodman says it exceeds legal requirements and will hold an information meeting after consulting the city. The dispute follows Goodman's withdrawal of a similar Sydney project after local resistance, and tests the Japan Data Center Council's May guidelines on community consultation.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.bio: Founded 2021 in San Francisco by Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and other former OpenAI researchers. Develops the Claude family of large language models. Privately held; major investors include Amazon and Google.
entities.desc: **NTT Data nears deal for first dedicated Japan data center (#137, Nikkei Asia Oct 13, 2026):** Anthropic is in final talks with NTT Data for an Osaka site of up to 500MW, costing up to ¥1tn to build before GPUs, with signing targeted by end-March 2027 and partial operation from 2028. It would be Anthropic's first facility in Japan built solely for it, adding to at least 14.8GW of compute it has signed since October 2025, mostly in the US. Japan demand comes from enterprise deals such as Hitachi's May rollout of Claude to about 290,000 staff. **Nippan confirms bulk book sales to Anthropic (#132, Oct 6-7, 2026):** Nippan Group Holdings told the Japan Book Publishers Association a group company sold large volumes of books to Anthropic between December 2024 and December 2025; the association asked it to stop supplying books for AI training. The episode follows Tokyo's voluntary training-data 'Principles Code' (Aug 25).

tags.l: NTT Data Osaka DC, up to 500MW (Oct 13)
Hitachi rolls out Claude to ~290k staff (May)

entities.name: Japan Exchange Group (JPX)
entities.bio: Formed in January 2013 by the merger of the Tokyo Stock Exchange and Osaka Securities Exchange. Operates the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Osaka Exchange and the JPX Market Innovation & Research unit, which calculates TOPIX. Listed on the TSE Prime market.
entities.desc: **TOPIX overhaul and Kioxia float change (#133, Oct 7, 2026):** JPX's periodic review raised Kioxia's TOPIX free-float ratio from 15% to 50% in two steps (end-October, end-November), triggering an estimated ¥2tn-3tn of passive buying, and confirmed which constituents fail the index's new size and trading-value tests; their weights shrink in stages from late October 2026 to July 2028. Roughly ¥160tn of assets track TOPIX, so JPX's index rules now move AI and chip stocks as much as company news.

tags.l: Next-gen TOPIX phase-out runs to July 2028

entities.name: Shibaura Machine
entities.bio: Founded 1938 and headquartered in Numazu, Shizuoka; operated for decades as Toshiba Machine before leaving the Toshiba group and renaming itself Shibaura Machine in 2020. Makes machine tools, injection and die-casting machines, precision machinery and industrial robots. Listed on the TSE Prime market.
entities.desc: **Ramps output to clear an AI-driven backlog (#134, Oct 2026):** Nikkei reported Japan's machine tool order backlog has passed ¥1 trillion on AI-related demand and that Shibaura Machine plans to raise production by about 50% to work through it. The same week JMTBA reported record September orders of ¥223.2bn (+60.4% y/y), with foreign orders a record ¥159.3bn. **Moore Nanotechnology acquisition (June 2026):** Agreed to buy US ultra-precision machine tool maker Moore Nanotechnology Systems, adding optics and precision-machining capability.

entities.name: Kyocera
entities.bio: Founded 1959 in Kyoto by Kazuo Inamori as Kyoto Ceramic. Makes fine ceramic semiconductor packages and substrates, electronic components, cutting tools and industrial equipment. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (6971).
entities.desc: **Tungsten carbide recycling line (#135, Oct 9, 2026):** will build a smelting line at its Kagoshima Sendai plant in Satsumasendai to recover tungsten carbide from used cutting tools using an amino-acid-based process, starting FY2030. METI certified the project under its critical-minerals supply-security program and Jiji reports a ¥3B subsidy. The move responds to China's tungsten export controls, which cut carbide and powder shipments to Japan to zero in Feb-Apr 2026 and tripled carbide prices.

entities.name: NICT (National Institute of Information and Communications Technology)
entities.desc: National research institute under the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications that holds Japan's largest Japanese-language web corpus and runs the WISDOM X question-answering system. **Active evaluation platform (#139, Oct 14, 2026):** with PFN and Sakura Internet, NICT will put a 能動的評価基盤 (active evaluation platform) into service from next fiscal year. Instead of testing models against a fixed prompt set that developers can train on, it keeps generating new high-risk prompts and checks outputs against web evidence. Prototypes: WISDOM-AR (generates risky prompts and judges answers for discrimination, crime facilitation or fraud) and WISDOM-CE (flags hallucination and bias by cross-checking web pages). NICT built a 200-billion-parameter LLM with PFN for the work, drawing on about 20 years of collected Japanese web data.

tags.l: Active AI evaluation platform to launch next FY
~20 years of Japanese web data; WISDOM X
No disclosed budget or procurement role

entities.name: Ricoh
entities.bio: Founded in 1936 in Tokyo by Kiyoshi Ichimura as a maker of photosensitive paper spun out of the RIKEN research institute. Grew into a global office-equipment and printing company and now sells document workflow and IT services to Japanese companies through Ricoh Japan. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
entities.desc: **Japanese document model on a Chinese base (#140, Oct 15, 2026):** Released Ricoh LMM_35B-A3B, a mixture-of-experts multimodal model with about 35 billion total and 3 billion active parameters, a 256K-token context and image and video input. Ricoh built it by applying its own reinforcement and curriculum learning to Alibaba's open Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. On Ricoh's JDocQA-Reasoning v2.0 benchmark it scored 0.841, level with the dense Qwen3.6-27B and above a commercial GPT-5.6 tier (0.821); its success rate on SB Intuitions' j-tau-bench telecom scenario rose to 77.7% from 62.4%. An NVFP4 version runs on one NVIDIA DGX Spark. It joins the RICOH on-premises LLM starter kit from November. **On-premises LLM line:** Released dense 27B and 9B multimodal models in June 2026 and built a reasoning multimodal model under METI's GENIAC phase 3.

tags.l: LMM_35B-A3B: 3B active params, on-prem from Nov

entities.name: Nidec
entities.bio: Founded in 1973 in Kyoto by Shigenobu Nagamori and three colleagues as a maker of small precision motors, later the leading supplier of hard-disk spindle motors. Expanded through dozens of acquisitions into automotive, appliance and industrial motors and drives, and changed its Japanese name from 日本電産 to ニデック in 2023. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
entities.desc: **Liability findings (#140, Oct 16, 2026):** An executive responsibility committee set up in March 2026 concluded that nine current and former officers can be held liable for damages over group-wide accounting irregularities, including founder Shigenobu Nagamori, former chairman Hiroshi Kobe, three former presidents and the CFO from May 2022 to March 2026. Nidec said it will consider legal action including damages claims and plans to publish a redacted report around Oct 20. **Scandal and losses:** A third-party report in March 2026 found irregularities across every business segment, driven by unrealistic targets; FY2025 (to March 2026) brought a ¥519 billion operating loss and ¥632 billion of impairments, and PwC Japan issued a disclaimer of opinion. A September 2026 probe found 844 improper quality practices, 60 of them serious. **Leadership turnover:** Nagamori left the board in December 2025; president Mitsuya Kishida resigned Sept 29, 2026 and was replaced by Michio Kaida.

entities.name: Omron
entities.bio: Founded 1933 in Osaka by Kazuma Tateishi as Tateisi Electric; headquartered in Kyoto. Makes factory automation controllers, sensors, safety components and robots (Industrial Automation is its largest segment), plus healthcare devices such as blood pressure monitors. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (6645).
entities.desc: **Buys OnLogic for $675M to build physical AI hardware (#141, Oct 13, 2026):** Agreed to acquire Interlogic, parent of US rugged industrial PC maker OnLogic, for $675M on an enterprise-value basis, funded mainly with cash; Interlogic had FY2025 net sales of $154.2M and EBITDA of $22.6M ($27.1M adjusted), about 30x EBITDA. OnLogic keeps its brand, direct build-to-order sales model and CEO Sean Larkin; over 90% of its sales are in the Americas and Europe. Omron plans to pair OnLogic's edge computers with its own controllers, sensors and robots to sell physical AI platforms and widen its US customer base; closing expected around January 2027. **Comau collaboration (May 2026):** Omron Robotics signed a deal with Italy's Comau to develop industrial automation systems.

tags.l: Edge PCs + controllers for physical AI
Rich price for a $154M-sales PC maker

entities.name: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry)
entities.bio: Founded 1974 in Taipei by Terry Gou; chairman Young Liu. The world's largest contract electronics manufacturer, assembling iPhones and Nvidia AI servers, and owner of Japan's Sharp since 2016. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2317).
entities.desc: **Takes 50% of Mitsubishi Electric's auto equipment unit (#141, Oct 16, 2026):** Its investment arm Lin Yin International Investment will pay ¥115bn for half of Mitsubishi Electric Mobility, a business with ¥875.6bn of annual sales in electrified powertrains, motors and control software, with closing expected October 2027. The deal gives Foxconn's contract EV business a Tier 1 supplier with established Japanese automaker relationships. **Japan EV push:** Signed a final agreement in January 2026 to set up a bus maker with Mitsubishi Fuso in Japan.

tags.l: Buys 50% of Mitsubishi Electric Mobility for ¥115bn

entities.name: MIC (Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications)
entities.desc: Ministry overseeing telecoms, broadcasting, local government and data infrastructure policy. **Data center and cloud certification (#143, Nikkei Oct 19, 2026):** Co-designing with METI a national security certification for data center operators and cloud providers serving Japan, assessing ownership/business details, leak safeguards and equipment suppliers on IPA's JC-STAR basis. Banks, hospitals and other holders of sensitive personal data would be urged to use certified services from after FY2027; a January 2027 Economic Security Promotion Act amendment would require prior notification by important-data holders and allow suspension orders. Expected in practice to exclude Chinese-controlled providers, citing China's National Intelligence Law.

tags.l: Econ. Security Act amendment, Jan 2027 Diet

entities.name: Dai-ichi Life Group
entities.bio: Founded in 1902 in Tokyo as Japan's first mutual life insurer, Dai-ichi Life demutualized and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2010, later reorganizing under a holding company now named Dai-ichi Life Group. It is one of Japan's largest life insurers and owns overseas units including TAL in Australia and Protective Life in the US.
entities.desc: Japanese life insurer expanding abroad as population decline shrinks its home market. **Bid for Challenger (#143, Oct 19, 2026):** Through TAL Dai-ichi Life Australia, made an indicative, non-binding A$11.80/share proposal for the ~79.6% of Challenger, Australia's largest annuity seller, it does not own, valuing Challenger at ~A$7.94B (US$5.5B), a 19.8% premium; it holds 20.36% after buying 15.1% from MS&AD in April 2025 at ~A$8.46. Conditional on due diligence, a scheme agreement, regulatory approval and a shareholder vote; Challenger's board is considering it. Rising JGB yields (10Y 2.91% on Oct 19) improve domestic bond returns but do not replace shrinking domestic premiums.

entities.name: GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae
entities.zh: GMOサイバーセキュリティ byイエラエ
entities.py: Jī Emu Ō Saibā Sekyuriti bai Ierae
entities.bio: Tokyo white-hat security firm that began as Ierae Security and became part of GMO Internet Group (TSE: 9449) in 2022, taking its current name. It sells penetration testing, vulnerability assessment and incident response, and runs a cybercrime countermeasures center led by former Interpol investigator Daiki Fukumori.
entities.desc: **Ties Chinese AI agent ARTEX to Japan breach wave (#144, Oct 19-20, 2026):** analyzed six overseas attack servers active Sept 18 to Oct 18 and found traces of ARTEX, an open-source Chinese penetration-testing agent that chains LLMs such as Claude, GPT and DeepSeek, on all six. One infrastructure targeted about 20 Japanese companies, nine in the same industry, and eight targets disclosed leaks in the past two months; sectors hit included e-commerce, finance, retail, logistics, media, education and marketing. CrowdStrike tied the same tool to breaches at 16 Korean financial institutions. Findings shared with law enforcement; no actor named.

tags.l: ARTEX AI agent traced on 6 attack servers (Oct 19)
Same tool hit 16 Korean financial firms

entities.name: Information-technology Promotion Agency (IPA)
entities.desc: **AI-driven attack simulation team (#147, Oct 23, 2026):** METI Minister Akazawa said IPA will stand up a team in November that uses AI to attack Japanese organisations' own systems in simulation so they can fix weaknesses before criminals find them. The plan follows a wave of breaches at Japanese companies in October and coincided with the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618/109619), which led SoftBank to suspend emergency alert texts and MUFG, Nomura, ANA and JR East to pull online services. **JC-STAR label:** IPA runs the JC-STAR IoT security labelling scheme that METI and MIC plan to build on for a national data center and cloud certification (#143). METI's IT and cybersecurity agency; also runs Japan's national IT engineer examinations.
